title: 8 ‘Pray like a Viking!’ Popularising Norse Mythology and Religion in Video Games with Historical Settings: The Case of Assassin’s Creed Valhalla (2020)
venue: Popularising the Middle Ages in Modern Fantasy
publisher: D. S. Brewer is an imprint of Boydell & Brewer Ltd
ai_summary: This chapter examines how Assassin's Creed Valhalla (2020) popularises Norse mythology and religion within a historically set video game, assessing how its depiction of pagan belief and Viking culture shapes players' understanding of the Middle Ages.

title: A intersecção entre história pública e indústria cultural nos videogames
venue: Práticas da História. Journal on Theory, Historiography and Uses of the Past
ai_summary: This Portuguese-language article argues that Public History and Culture Industry theory intersect in video games, treating the game as a commodity that shapes historical representation under market logic. It tests this through case studies of the Civilization and Age of Empires strategy series and the Assassin's Creed franchise.

title: A Matter of Accessibility: A Guidelines-Based Accessibility Evaluation of Award-Nominated Video Games
ai_summary: This study audits five Game Awards 2025 accessibility-nominated titles, including Assassin's Creed Shadows, against the 121-item Game Accessibility Guidelines, finding high implementation rates overall but low documentation and uneven compliance, especially for blind players and advanced guidelines.

title: Agitation System in Assassin's Creed Nexus
topics: Game AI, Rendering & Computational Methods; Game mechanism
ai_summary: The paper presents the Agitation System developed for Assassin's Creed Nexus VR, which gives non-player characters a temporary memory of the player's actions and uses an intensity-based value to shape their responses and heighten realism in virtual reality.

title: Alcibiades’ Political Bisexuality in Assassin’s Creed: Odyssey (Ubisoft Quebéc, 2018)
ai_summary: The paper argues that Assassin's Creed: Odyssey draws on ancient sources on Alcibiades to portray his bisexuality not merely as a character trait but as a political tool shaped by the instabilities of Athenian politics during the Peloponnesian War.

title: Analyzing Islamophobia in Video Games: A Case Study of Assassin’s Creed Mirage and Cultural Strategies of Resistance in Islamic Societies
ai_summary: The paper argues that Assassin's Creed Mirage reproduces a distorted image of Islam and Muslims through cognitive distortion and emotional-affective provocation, redefining concepts such as jihad, justice, worship, and martyrdom within violent and sectarian contexts, and it proposes media literacy, indigenous content development, and cultural cooperation among Muslim societies as countermeasures.

title: Animaux du quotidien et animaux mythiques, des textes anciens au monde vidéoludique: Figuration de l’animal à travers le jeu Assassin’s Creed Odyssey (Ubisoft, 2018)
venue: La bête, le Bien et le Mal - Figures mythiques et incarnations de l’animal, de l’Antiquité à nos jours
publisher: Centre pour la Communication Scientifique Directe
ai_summary: This paper examines how animal figures from ancient Greek myth, including the Ceryneian hind, the Cretan bull, Lycaon and Callisto as animals, and hybrid creatures, are adapted in Assassin's Creed Odyssey, analyzing the game's treatment of hunting, lethality, humanity in animals, and the ally/enemy dichotomy against textual, archaeological, and iconographic sources.

title: Architecture as an Object of Artistic Interpretation in Game Design
ai_summary: The paper argues that architecture in action video games, including the Assassin's Creed series, Bloodborne, BioShock, and Deus Ex: Mankind Divided, is an artistic language rather than mere backdrop, and it classifies the techniques (reconstruction, stylization, hyperbolization, hybridization, and pastiche) by which games rework historical monuments while preserving their recognizable features.

title: Assassin's Creed Valhalla Oyunu İncelemesi Üzerinden, Görsel Sanatlar Bağlamında 3D Oyun Karakterleri Oluşturma Süreçleri
ai_summary: This Turkish-language study examines the 3D character and costume design of Assassin's Creed Valhalla through the lens of graphic and visual arts, arguing that visual elements such as line, form, texture, color, and light build the psychological and emotional bond between player and character, and that the game functions as an interactive artwork shaped by both historical research and technical constraints.

title: Assassin’s Creed Odyssey
venue: Characters and Characterization in Mythological Video Games
ai_summary: This monograph examines how mythological characters are characterized across six games, including Assassin's Creed Odyssey, arguing that games transform Greco-Roman, Norse, and Egyptian myths through a dialogue and play with antiquity that yields diverse 'languages' of mythology reception.

title: Beyond Kratos
venue: A Humanities Pedagogy Approach to Modern Masculinity
ai_summary: This Routledge chapter argues that game mechanics, such as purchasable sexual services and gendered access restrictions, construct and reproduce masculinity across four franchises, including Assassin's Creed, and it advocates using these games in classroom discussions of gender and male identity.

title: Brothels, Buffs, and Breeding
venue: The Routledge Companion to Video Games and History
ai_summary: This chapter examines how historical games with premodern settings, including the Assassin's Creed series, Kingdom Come: Deliverance, Pentiment, and Crusader Kings, depict romantic and sexual relationships, arguing that they typically impose modern progressive attitudes on gender and sexuality, which mutes historical homophobia and misogyny and introduces modern prejudices.

title: Characters and Characterization in Mythological Video Games
ai_summary: This monograph, the first book-length study of mythology reception in video games, uses narratology, game studies, and classical reception to examine how six games (Smite, Assassin's Creed Odyssey, Immortals Fenyx Rising, God of War, Theseus, and Asgard's Wrath 2) characterize mythological figures, and argues that these games display diverse 'languages' of mythology reception rooted in a continuous dialogue and play with antiquity.

title: Commercial Video Games as Playable Spatial Models in Urban Geography Education: An Exploratory Mixed-Methods Case Study
ai_summary: This exploratory mixed-methods case study in a German upper-secondary geography course uses Assassin's Creed Odyssey Discovery Tour and SimCity BuildIt as playable spatial models, finding gains in model application and critique, though causal claims and retention remain unestablished, and proposes seven testable design principles for geography teaching.

title: COMPUTER GAMES IN THE EDUCATIONAL ENVIRONMENT: STUDYING HISTORY THROUGH GAME TECHNOLOGIES (USING THE EXAMPLE OF THE 8TH GRADE)
authors: Sabaev, Semyon Sergeevich; Игоревич, Левин Никита
ai_summary: The article examines how computer games can support history teaching in eighth-grade classrooms, using the Assassin's Creed series as a case study of game-based technology, and concludes that game-based excursions are worth integrating into the curriculum when supported by methodological guidance and critical analysis of game content.

title: Conclusion
venue: Characters and Characterization in Mythological Video Games
topics: Mythology & Classical Reception; Semiotics & Character Analysis
ai_summary: This concluding chapter of a monograph on mythology in video games argues that games such as Assassin's Creed Odyssey transform Greco-Roman and other mythological characters through characterization and player participation, forming a dialogic, playful relationship with antiquity and a diverse set of mythological 'languages' of reception.

title: CULTURAL TOURISM DESTINATIONS THROUGH THE WORLD OF VIDEO GAMES – A CASE STUDY OF FLORENCE AND VENICE IN ASSASSIN'S CREED II
venue: Journal of Innovations in Business and Industry
ai_summary: This case study argues that Assassin's Creed II presents Florence and Venice in a detailed, historically credible, and immersive way, strengthening players' emotional connection to these destinations and suggesting that video games have promotional value for tourism marketing and policy.

title: Dijital Oyunların Kültürel Mirasın Tanıtılmasına Katkısı: 'Assassin’s Creed Revelations' Örneği
ai_summary: This Turkish-language case study of Assassin's Creed Revelations examines how the game visualizes 16th-century Istanbul's mosques, walls, and towers, arguing that its interactive exploration can introduce players to cultural heritage and make it a useful tool for public heritage promotion.

title: Discussion: Mythology in Games
venue: Characters and Characterization in Mythological Video Games
topics: Mythology & Classical Reception; Semiotics & Character Analysis
ai_summary: This book chapter examines how mythological characters are characterized in video games, using narratological and classical reception frameworks to analyze six case studies, including Assassin's Creed Odyssey, and argues that games engage with antiquity through dialogue and play.

title: El Antiguo Egipto: análisis de una intervención didáctica en Educación Secundaria a través del videojuego Assassin’s Creed Origins
venue: Repositorio Institucional de la Universidad de Huelva (Universidad de Huelva)
topics: Game-Based Learning & Pedagogy; Player Experience & Affect
ai_summary: This Spanish-language thesis presents an action-research case study in which a first-year Compulsory Secondary Education class learned about ancient Egypt through the story mode of Assassin's Creed Origins, and it concludes that the game improved student motivation, historical understanding, and participation, offering good-practice indicators for teachers.

title: Encountering the Sacred Past: Religious Experience and Historical Empathy in Assassin’s Creed Valhalla
ai_summary: This article argues that Assassin's Creed Valhalla can support historical empathy by showing how Norse and Christian religious frameworks shaped people's worldviews in Viking Age England and Norway, but that its historical simplifications and gameplay-driven adaptations require teacher scaffolding and critical reflection, so the game should be treated as entertainment rather than a faithful representation of the past.

title: Flouting Maxims and Pragmatic Equivalence in the English–Indonesian Translation of “Assassin’s Creed: Shadows”
authors: Ekadandi, I. Gusti Ngurah Agung; Hikmaharyanti, Putu Desi Anggerina
venue: ELYSIAN JOURNAL : English Literature, Linguistics and Translation Studies
ai_summary: This study examines how characters in Assassin's Creed: Shadows deliberately flout Grice's conversational maxims to convey sarcasm, tension, power dynamics, and unspoken emotion, and argues that these implied meanings are largely preserved in the Indonesian translation through communicative equivalence.

title: Freie Titelübersetzung: <<The>> portrayal of Catholicism in Assassin’s Creed Brotherhood
ai_summary: This German-language paper argues that Assassin's Creed Brotherhood portrays Catholicism mainly through its institutional, political, and power-related dimensions, with corruption and violence as central conflicts, while specific religious beliefs and practices play a much smaller role, producing a fictionalized interpretation of historical and religious references rather than a historical reconstruction.

title: From Concept to Creation: Writers Are The Builders of Worlds
ai_summary: The paper argues that the Assassin's Creed franchise succeeded in games through integrated, collaborative worldbuilding that blends real history with the Animus lore, while its 2016 film adaptation failed by treating that worldbuilding as set dressing, and it offers these lessons for writing the screenplay of The Chemist.

title: From virtual exploration to real-world travel: A trait-conditioned stimulus-organism-response framework for game-induced tourism
ai_summary: Using survey data from 504 Assassin's Creed players, this dissertation tests a trait-conditioned Stimulus–Organism–Response model showing that spatial presence and exploratory flow drive place attachment and real-world visit intention, with player traits (Achievement, Narrative, Esthetic, Social) attenuating these pathways.

title: Historical Characters in Antiquity Games
venue: The Routledge Companion to Video Games and History
topics: Mythology & Classical Reception; Semiotics & Character Analysis
ai_summary: This chapter introduces character theory from literary and game studies and surveys historical figures in Greco-Roman antiquity games, then examines Socrates as a non-playable character in Assassin's Creed Odyssey and the player persona in Expeditions: Rome as case studies of how historical characters can be analyzed.

title: HISTÓRIA, CAPACITISMO E INCLUSÃO: A UTILIZAÇÃO DE VIDEOGAMES E MÉTODOS DE FÁCIL LEITURA COMO FERRAMENTAS DE ENSINO-APRENDIZAGEM
tags: #source/auto-retrieved; game:origins; game:other-games; game:valhalla; lang:pt; rel:case-study; type:research-article
ai_summary: The paper argues that combining accessible technologies, including Assassin's Creed: Discovery Tour, Easy-to-Read methods (FALEAC), and Vygotskian pedagogical strategies can counter ableism and make historical learning in higher education more inclusive and engaging.

title: Humanistic Practice Between Virtuality and Reality: An Analysis of the Humanistic Value and Realization Paths of Digital Spaces Based on AAA Game Case Studies
venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
ai_summary: This paper argues that AAA game environments, using Black Myth: Wukong, the Assassin's Creed series, and Ghost of Tsushima as case studies, can carry humanistic value through spatial aesthetics, environmental storytelling, and sense of place, while noting tensions between commercial logic and humanistic care and between historical accuracy and subjective authenticity.

title: Introduction
venue: Characters and Characterization in Mythological Video Games
topics: Mythology & Classical Reception; Semiotics & Character Analysis
ai_summary: This introduction to a Bloomsbury monograph establishes a narratological framework for characterization in video games and presents six case studies of mythological characters, including Assassin's Creed Odyssey, to argue that games engage with antiquity and other mythologies through dialogue and play.

title: Jeux vidéo et histoire de la psychiatrie. La difficulté de sortir des stéréotypes et de l’histoire
venue: RiMe. Rivista dell'Istituto di Storia dell'Europa Mediterranea
ai_summary: Using a semiotic approach, this article examines how three self-proclaimed historical video games (Outlast, Assassin's Creed: Syndicate, and Town of Light) represent the history of psychiatry, arguing that they often reproduce hegemonic institutional and biomedical narratives while struggling to give voice to marginalized, non-hegemonic perspectives.

title: La ciudad reinterpretada: arquitectura, identidad urbana y representación en los videojuegos
ai_summary: This thesis examines how video games reinterpret real cities through architecture and urban planning, comparing Grand Theft Auto V and Assassin's Creed Unity to show how spatial transformations turn physical cities into interactive digital environments.

title: La resurrección interactiva del pasado: videojuegos históricos en realidad virtual y epistemología de la inmersión
ai_summary: This Spanish-language article argues that VR historical games such as Assassin's Creed Discovery Tour function as programmable historiographical devices that both produce the illusion of immediate presence and expose the mediation of the past, thereby contributing to Digital Art History.

title: Labyrinth: Knossos, Myth and Reality
venue: The Oxford Handbook of Digital Classical Studies
ai_summary: This chapter examines the 2023 Ashmolean Museum exhibition Labyrinth: Knossos, Myth and Reality, a post-digital archaeological display that included an Assassin's Creed Odyssey video game experience alongside objects, 3D prints, and digital media, and uses visitor evaluation data to assess whether these digital elements shaped engagement with the exhibition and its objects.

title: Le rôle de la maîtrise de l’anglais dans l’apprentissage du francais : une étude de cas dans le cadre du jeu Assassin’s Creed Unity
authors: Gashmardi, Mahmoud Reza; Yazdian, Amir Reza
venue: Revue internationale des technologies en pédagogie universitaire
ai_summary: This French-language case study examines how English proficiency affects learning French within the context of Assassin's Creed Unity, treating the game as a tool for language acquisition. The abstract merely repeats the title, so the specific findings cannot be confirmed from the supplied material.

title: Localising Combat Ethics in Arabic: Narrative Framing, Martial Register, and Cultural Resonance in Assassin’s Creed Mirage
ai_summary: This article analyses the Arabic localisation of Assassin's Creed Mirage's three Creed tenets, finding semantic continuity with the English text and no explicit religious or classical moral terminology, and argues that furūsiyya and akhlāq are productive interpretive frameworks only when supported by marked language, recurring patterns, historical evidence, and multimodal context, proposing a graded evidential model for culturally informed localisation research.

title: Londres jugable : entre realidad y ficción : imaginarios urbanos y los motivos arquitectónicos en el videojuego
ai_summary: This thesis analyzes how London's urban space is represented in three open-world games, Assassin's Creed Syndicate, The Getaway: Black Monday, and Watch Dogs: Legion, using a spatial and iconographic analysis of architecture, urban atmosphere, mobility, and cityscape. It finds that none reproduces London literally and that each game generates a distinct urban imaginary (historical in Syndicate, formal in The Getaway, prospective in Watch Dogs: Legion), concluding that a less distorted representation depends on the balance between form, architectural character, and urban experience rather than visual resemblance alone.

title: Los videojuegos como caballo de Troya en la enseñanza de historia
ai_summary: This Spanish-language review of the edited volume Les Usages Pédagogiques des Jeux Vidéos Assassin's Creed (2023) examines how Assassin's Creed games can be used to teach history in schools, and it proposes a comparable pedagogical experience for the Mexican context.

title: Mapping the Global Multimedia Value Chain of Assassin’s Creed: Shadows (2021–2025)
authors: Akbar, Ahmad Taufik; Adrian, Stefan Risky; Sirhadi, Dharma; Purbantina, Adiasri Putri
venue: Global Economic, Social, and Development Review
ai_summary: This case study maps the global production network behind Assassin's Creed: Shadows (2021–2025), showing how Ubisoft Québec coordinates more than fifteen studios across three continents and how support functions such as archiving, education, and sustainability sustain the game's cultural authenticity and long-term value.

title: O SAMURAI NEGRO EM ASSASSIN'S CREED SHADOWS: UMA ANÁLISE DO DISCURSO GAMER SOBRE A “LACRAÇÃO” NOS VIDEOGAMES
venue: Da contagem à crítica: estudos bibliométricos e de linguagens
ai_summary: This Portuguese-language paper examines gamer discourse around the 'woke' ("lacração") debate surrounding the Black samurai character Yasuke in Assassin's Creed Shadows, analyzing how race and representation in the game are contested within online player communities. Note: the supplied abstract describes a bibliometric and translation-studies volume (GETTEC) and does not match the paper's title, so the classification relies on the title alone.

title: Playable Masculinity : A qualitative study of Yasuke's portrayal and ludic design in Assassin's Creed Shadows
authors: Davidsson, Arvid Nolenstam; Lagerqvist, Filip Ynner
ai_summary: This Swedish-language qualitative study uses close playing of 30 hours of Assassin's Creed Shadows, analyzed through Pérez Latorre's ludic rule types, Hall's encoding/decoding model, and Connell's hegemonic masculinity, to argue that Yasuke's rule-based design systematically equates masculinity with violence, power, and physical dominance and steers players toward a dominant reading.

title: Playing America: Myth, Memory, and National Identity in Historical Video Games
venue: Edinburgh Napier Research Repository (Edinburgh Napier University)
ai_summary: This chapter argues that historical video games, including Assassin's Creed III, Red Dead Redemption 2, and The Oregon Trail, reproduce hegemonic American national myths of freedom, frontier expansion, and individualism while marginalising histories of slavery, colonialism, and racial violence.

title: Popularising the Middle Ages in Modern Fantasy: Neomedievalism, Video Games, and Vikings
editors: Schwarz, Angela; Larrington, Carolyne; Braun, Charlotte; Velten, Hans Rudolf; Young, Helen; Schrage, Lukas; Weber, Milan; Su, Minjie; Specht, Theresa; Winnerling, Tobias; Pinsker, Tom; Larrington, Carolyne; Velten, Hans Rudolf; Young, Helen
ai_summary: This edited volume examines how gritty neomedievalism in popular culture, including Assassin's Creed Valhalla alongside film, television, literature, and manga, draws its appeal from claims of authenticity and engages with debates on identity, race, gender, and fan reception.

title: Religious Tensions: The Itatehyōzu Shrine in Assassin’s Creed Shadows
venue: UEA Digital Repository (University of East Anglia)
ai_summary: This paper examines the controversy over the possibility of destroying the Itatehyōzu Shrine in Assassin's Creed Shadows, analyzing from historical and political science perspectives how differing Japanese and Western views on race, history, and religion help explain the backlash.

title: Report on Qualitative Analysis of Games and Gamers
authors: Yodovich, Neta; Gislam, Charlotte; Bagnall, Gaynor; Crawford, Garry
venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
ai_summary: This University of Salford report uses surveys, interviews, and case studies of Disco Elysium, the Assassin's Creed series, and 80 Days to argue that empathy in video games is a relational, reflective, and contextual process shaped by the interaction between game, player, and social context rather than by mechanics or genre alone.

title: Representation, Resistance, and Moderation: The Politics of Review Bombing in Assassin's Creed Shadows
authors: Baltar, Alan Tapscott; Villanueva, Jordi Justicia; Pujol, Ona Anglada; Rota, Mercè Oliva
ai_summary: This preliminary study examines the review bombing campaign against Assassin's Creed Shadows, arguing that user reviews became a site of political and cultural contestation over the game's representation of an Afro-American samurai, a female ninja, and queer relationships, and over the discourses of authenticity and 'wokeness' that framed the polarized reaction.

title: Seen But Not Played
venue: The Routledge Companion to Video Games and History
ai_summary: This chapter examines how Assassin's Creed Origins, set in late Ptolemaic Egypt, portrays children, including their roles, physical depiction, and the worlds built around them, and argues that games should include children in historical settings to reconstruct ancient childhood.

title: Sounding Cultural Identity: Representing Japan and the Nordic Region in Video Game Music
ai_summary: This thesis uses Thomas B. Yee's framework of cultural width and depth to compare how video game music represents Japanese and Nordic identity in Ghost of Yōtei, Sekiro: Shadows Die Twice, Assassin's Creed Valhalla, and Valheim, finding that cultural identity is conveyed through recognizable sonic signifiers rather than strict historical authenticity, with internally produced games integrating culturally specific features more deeply than externally produced ones.

title: Teaching mythology with video games: two workshops for secondary education
topics: Game-Based Learning & Pedagogy; Mythology & Classical Reception
ai_summary: The article argues that video games can support mythology education and presents two classroom workshops for Flemish secondary students: one using Smite to design a mythological character, and one using the Story Creator in Assassin's Creed Odyssey to explore different modes of engaging with Greco-Roman myth, with practical guidance on organising such workshops.

title: The promise of freedom in historical games
authors: Mol, Angus A. A.; Politopoulos, Aris; Lammes, Sybille
topics: History Memory; Philosophy & Ontology of Game Worlds
ai_summary: Mol, Politopoulos, and Lammes use Graeber and Wengrow's three forms of freedom (movement, disobedience, and creation) to examine how Sid Meier's Civilization and the Assassin's Creed series depict and make interactive revolutions and radical historical change, and how far these games' promise of playful past-engagement limits genuine historical exploration.

title: THE ROLE OF VIDEO GAMES IN EDUCATION: THE CASE OF ASSASSIN’S CREED
venue: Çukurova Üniversitesi Sosyal Bilimler Enstitüsü Dergisi
ai_summary: The paper argues that Assassin's Creed Odyssey's Discovery Tour: Ancient Greece uses narrative design and historical reconstruction to foster educational engagement, identifying authenticity, agency, historical empathy, and accessibility as the core pedagogical dimensions through which students can experience history as an interpretive process.

title: TRANSLATING HISTORY BEYOND LANGUAGE: OTTOMAN ISTANBUL IN ASSASSIN’S CREED REVELATIONS
authors: Şeker, Osman Rüçhan; Okyayuz, A. Ş.
venue: Kafkas Universitesi Sosyal Bilimler Enstitüsü Dergisi
ai_summary: The paper argues that Assassin's Creed: Revelations can be read as a multimodal and intersemiotic translation that rewrites Ottoman Istanbul through visual and auditory resources, using Peirce's semiotics, Lefevere's rewriting theory, and Said's Orientalism to show how its representations of the market, courtyard, Janissary, belly dancers, and minarets produce ideologically shaped historical meaning.

title: Transmission of folklore meanings in the virtual reality of a video game
venue: Taras Shevchenko National University of Kyiv
games: Black Flag; Odyssey; Other games; Valhalla
topics: Game-Based Learning & Pedagogy; Mythology & Classical Reception
tags: #source/openalex; game:black-flag; game:odyssey; game:other-games; game:valhalla; lang:other; rel:case-study; type:thesis
ai_summary: This Ukrainian-language dissertation examines how folklore, mythology, and traditional culture are transmitted into the virtual worlds of a selection of video games, including Assassin's Creed IV: Black Flag, Assassin's Creed: Odyssey, and Assassin's Creed: Valhalla, and assesses their potential for popularizing cultural heritage and supporting learning.

title: Un nuevo mercado para turistas jóvenes: explorando la relación entre los videojuegos y el turismo cultural y de patrimonio histórico
ai_summary: This Spanish-language thesis argues that videogame-induced travel is a contemporary form of the Grand Tour impulse, combining a historical comparison of tourism, a typology of game-tourism mechanisms, and a survey of 82 young travelers that finds the Assassin's Creed franchise produced the broadest range of destination associations of any single game series.

title: Video games and place branding: A netnographic study of Assassin’s Creed Shadows
authors: Tuomi, Aarni; Abidin, Husna Zainal; Ascenção, M.
ai_summary: A netnographic and survey study of Assassin's Creed Shadows examines whether the game's depiction of Wakayama Prefecture can support inbound tourism, finding that players already plan real-life trips and that stakeholders favor game-themed offerings if local heritage and residents' daily lives are protected, and it proposes 'prospect-based authenticity' as a new way to understand tourists' desire to validate imagined experiences.

title: Virtual antiquity: ‘the closest thing to a time machine that lets you experience ancient Greece’
ai_summary: The article examines how developers, scholars, and players use the metaphor of time travel to describe simulations of the ancient world, which the author calls 'virtual antiquity', using Meta's metaverse campaign, the Virtual Reality Oracle, and Assassin's Creed Odyssey as case studies. It argues that the metaphor does not literally transport players to the past but instead expands the boundaries of how history can be represented.

title: Visibility Without Agency
tags: #source/auto-retrieved; game:ac3; game:origins; game:other-games; lang:en; rel:core; type:research-article
ai_summary: The article examines how racial minorities are represented in Assassin's Creed III, Origins, and Liberation, combining semiotic and narrative analysis of the games with thematic analysis of Reddit and YouTube comments. It argues that these representations often reinforce westernized worldviews, while players from diverse cultural backgrounds embrace, challenge, or reframe them, showing how games shape cultural memory, identity, and power.

title: VİDEO OYUNLARINDA MEKANSAL TASARIMIN İNCELENMESI: YÖNTEMLER, İLHAM KAYNAKLARI VE YORUMLAMA
ai_summary: This Turkish-language thesis argues that virtual cities in open-world games are computationally constructed spatial systems rather than simple copies of real cities, using interviews with 20 professionals and comparative analysis of Assassin's Creed Unity (mimetic, historically reconstructed architecture) and Grand Theft Auto V (ludic, flow-oriented navigation) to show a fidelity–flow paradox and the principle of selective fidelity.

title: Zwischen Education und Entertainment – Eine spielerische Entdeckungstour durch die griechische Antike
ai_summary: This German-language paper examines how Assassin's Creed Odyssey's Discovery Tour turns the game's historical settings of ancient Greece into educational content, analyzing the tensions between commercial, technical, and scholarly demands in production and assessing the potential and limits of such learning games in historical education through a structural analysis and an empirical study.

title: ЛОКАЛИЗАЦИИ ВИДЕОИГР: К ВОПРОСУ ОБ ОГРАНИЧЕНИЯХ И ИХ ВЛИЯНИИ НА ПЕРЕВОДЧЕСКОЕ РЕШЕНИЕ
venue: Вестник Тверского государственного университета Серия Филология
ai_summary: The paper examines how external constraints in video game localization, such as character limits, voice-over synchronization, and genre conventions, narrow translators' choices and make localization a functionally and audiovisually determined process within the multimodal structure of the game, using official Russian localizations of The Witcher 3, Cyberpunk 2077, Skyrim, Assassin's Creed Valhalla, and The Last of Us Part I.

title: ‘Interact with History Like Never Before’
venue: The Routledge Companion to Video Games and History
topics: Game mechanism; History Memory; Transmedia Adaptation
ai_summary: This chapter identifies four emergent possibilities in historical game mods (pastiche and parody, transmedia storytelling, extended history, and systemic advantage) and argues that modding, including the Assassin's Creed Odyssey community's repurposing of its Story Creator Mode, enables players to interact with history in new ways and can foster historical thinking.

title: “…It's Really Pathetic Seeing a Grown Man Cry”
venue: The Routledge Companion to Video Games and History
ai_summary: This chapter compares the depiction of masculinity in Assassin's Creed Valhalla and World of Warcraft, arguing that both games challenge essentialist views of gender while showing how claims of 'historical accuracy' are used to defend traditional notions of medieval manliness, a justification that players also contest.

title: ”La bella Italia!” : Peliympäristöjen koodautuminen historiallisiksi ja kaupunkien merkitys Assassin’s Creed II -videopelissä sekä niiden historiallisuuden tunnistaminen Pelit- ja Pelaaja-lehtien kirjoituksissa
ai_summary: This Finnish master's thesis examines how Assassin's Creed II (2009) encodes its Renaissance-era Northern Italian game environments as historical, through cultural layers, naturalized codes, and medievalism, and how Finnish gaming magazines Pelit and Pelaaja recognize that historicity in their reviews. It argues that the game's Renaissance is selectively authentic, blending historical cities, families, landmarks, and social classes with gameplay-driven fiction centered on Ezio Auditore.

title: A cultura da convergência e as relações intermidiáticas em 'Assassins's Creed'
authors: Oliveira, Laécio Fernandes de; Rodrigues, Linduarte Pereira
venue: Revista 2i | Estudos de Identidade e Intermedialidade
ai_summary: The paper examines how the Assassin's Creed franchise, beginning with the first game's reference to Vladimir Bartol's novel Alamut and extending to the 2016 film, illustrates transmedia and intermedial relations within convergence culture, arguing that cinema, video games, and the internet update a shared mythology and invite audience participation.

title: A Link to the Past : The Role of Videogames in Conveying and Generating Historical Information
ai_summary: This University of Turku thesis examines Assassin's Creed II, Kingdom Come: Deliverance, and Ghost of Tsushima to argue that history-based videogames can effectively teach historical information when epistemological and ethical considerations are addressed, and that they are valuable source material for historians studying the past and present.

title: A Study on Digital Game Cases Utilizing Cultural Heritage
authors: Wi, Sang-hee; Lee, Ji-Yun; Ahn, Hyoung-Ki
ai_summary: This Korean-language study examines digital games that use cultural heritage, including Mulaka, Black Myth: Wukong, Assassin's Creed Discovery Tour, and Black Desert, and argues that immersive storytelling, historical reconstruction, and interactivity help preserve and disseminate heritage. It also warns of historical distortion and over-commercialization, and calls for developer-historian collaboration and strategies that link educational content, tourism, and digital archiving, especially to spread Korean heritage through K-content.

title: Ancient Egypt in Video Games
editors: Cromwell, Jennifer
ai_summary: This edited volume examines how Ancient Egypt is represented across more than forty years of video games, from major franchises such as Assassin's Creed and Tomb Raider to independent titles, and shows how games shape popular imagination of Egyptian history, culture, and monuments.

title: Ancient Rome in the video game medium: The case of Marcus Junius Brutus for a reflection on myth and history
venue: Catalan Journal of Communication & Cultural Studies
tags: #source/auto-retrieved; game:ezio-trilogy; game:origins; game:other-games; lang:en; rel:case-study; type:research-article
ai_summary: This article examines how Marcus Junius Brutus is narratively and visually reshaped across Assassin's Creed: Brotherhood, Assassin's Creed: Origins, and Shadow of Rome, arguing that the transformation of Roman history into myth in these games, while driven by contemporary sensibilities, retains traceable roots in ancient sources that can aid interpretation of the past.

title: Assassin's Creed
authors: Chang, Edmond Y.; Welsh, Timothy J.
venue: Video Games, Literature, and Close Playing
ai_summary: This chapter uses Assassin's Creed (2016) to argue that the games industry's claim that technological power can fully transport players into a game's narrative and world is a fallacy, because video games constantly remind players that they are playing a game.

title: Assassin's Creed - Nottingham
venue: The Bulletin of the International Association for Robin Hood Studies
games: AC1; AC3; Black Flag; Ezio Trilogy; Odyssey; Origins; Other games; Syndicate; Unity; Valhalla
tags: #source/auto-retrieved; game:ac1; game:ac3; game:black-flag; game:ezio-trilogy; game:odyssey; game:origins; game:other-games; game:syndicate; game:unity; game:valhalla; lang:en; rel:core; type:research-article
ai_summary: The paper argues that the Assassin's Creed series models its player-characters and game mechanics on Eric Hobsbawm's concept of the Noble Robber, drawing parallels to the Robin Hood legend and suggesting that the series should prompt broader consideration of how that legend shapes representations of justice and communal benefit in video games.

title: Assassin's Creed Syndicate and the Depiction of Female "Britishness" in Victorian London
authors: Reid, Andrew James; Donald, Iain; Austin, Hailey J.; Pittner, Fruzsina
ai_summary: This paper analyzes how Assassin's Creed Syndicate depicts its lead and supporting female characters and how it reflects Victorian British identity, examining the game's blend of historical fiction and real nineteenth-century political and social change, including women's roles and agency.

title: Assassin’s Creed i klasserommet: En kvalitativ undersøkelse av elevers opplevelser av Discovery Tour i undervisningen om demokrati
ai_summary: A qualitative study based on semi-structured interviews with six Norwegian students, examining how they experienced using the Assassin's Creed Odyssey Discovery Tour to learn about democracy in social studies. Students' learning varied, shaped largely by their prior gaming familiarity, and the author concludes that meaningful learning requires more time to adapt to the game, ideally more than one class hour.

title: Assassin’s Creed: From Leap of Faith to Brand Value
games: AC1; AC3; Black Flag; Ezio Trilogy; Odyssey; Origins; Other games; Syndicate; Unity; Valhalla
tags: #source/auto-retrieved; game:ac1; game:ac3; game:black-flag; game:ezio-trilogy; game:odyssey; game:origins; game:other-games; game:syndicate; game:unity; game:valhalla; lang:en; rel:core; type:research-article
ai_summary: This study examines how brand identity and brand image, analysed through Kapferer's and Keller's models, together with monetisation and profitability data, sustain the commercial success of the Assassin's Creed franchise, finding a moderate correlation between reviews and revenue and a strong correlation between the number of versions (including DLCs) and total revenue.

title: Bayek’s promise: authentic vs. accurate Ptolemaic astronomy in Assassin’s Creed: Origins
ai_summary: The paper argues that Assassin's Creed: Origins integrates an archaeoastronomically informed account of Ptolemaic Egyptian astronomy into Bayek's personal character, presenting stargazing as an individual, lived practice that challenges top-down narratives of astronomy and connects players to a 'living' ancient Egypt.

title: Bridging Virtual and Real Gamification in Teaching Architectural Features With Assassin's Creed Odyssey
venue: European Conference on Games Based Learning
ai_summary: A two-group experiment with 20 participants compares learning about architectural features from Assassin's Creed Odyssey's Discovery Mode against reading a text transcript of the same narration, finding out whether immersive game-based exploration improves knowledge retention and spatial understanding for non-specialists.

title: Consumo de jogos e Neoliberalismo Progressista: os múltiplos usos do passado nas representações de Cleópatra
ai_summary: This Portuguese-language article compares how Cleopatra VII is represented across three films (1917, 1934, 1963) and Assassin's Creed Origins (2017), arguing that these portrayals shift with their production contexts under 'Progressive Neoliberalism' and the consumption of the past, with particular attention to the depiction of Black people.

title: Design de Jogos para Herança Cultural: Como os jogos comerciais ensinam sobre culturas
venue: Portuguese National Funding Agency for Science, Research and Technology (RCAAP Project by FCT)
ai_summary: This Portuguese-language dissertation examines how commercial game design can teach cultural heritage, combining a catalogue of cultural-transmission techniques, a case study of Assassin's Creed: Odyssey's main missions, and a survey of 55 participants who viewed videos illustrating those techniques.

title: Dialogue between Literature and Video Games on the Example of Slovenian Literature
ai_summary: This University of Maribor dissertation proposes a combined narratological and ludological framework for studying intermedial links between video games and Slovenian literature, classifies narrative games by their degree of narrative content, and analyzes Assassin's Creed (2007) and its relationship to Vladimir Bartol's novel Alamut as a case study of how game mechanics and narrative elements migrate into literary works.

title: Digital game-based learning: Does it improve university students’ learning in an online context?
authors: Chaves-yuste, Beatriz; De‑la‑peña, Cristina; Candel, Elena Carrión
venue: Knowledge Management & E-Learning An International Journal
ai_summary: This study evaluates a digital game-based learning intervention in an online university course, combining the serious games Socrative and Cerebriti with educational videos based on Assassin's Creed Odyssey, and reports that the approach significantly improved students' knowledge, engagement, and 21st-century competencies.

title: Directivity and Modifiability in video-game environments for learning. Two paradigmatic cases compared
authors: Sardo, Michele; Morreale, Domenico; Ugolini, Francesco Claudio
venue: Journal of Inclusive Methodology and Technology in Learning and Teaching
ai_summary: This paper proposes a theoretical framework for evaluating game-based learning environments through a qualitative comparison of Assassin's Creed Odyssey: Discovery Tour (low modifiability, open-world directivity) and Minecraft Education (high modifiability, constructionist design), and concludes that Minecraft's creativity requires teacher scaffolding while the Discovery Tour needs personalized and collaborative activities to offset its limited player expression.

title: DO BOM SELVAGEM AO WESTERN
ai_summary: This Portuguese-language article examines whether the racist stereotypes of Native Americans built by European colonizers and later perpetuated by Hollywood appear in the Assassin's Creed franchise, comparing its indigenous characters and historical events with those established stereotypes.

title: El tópico de ombra y su función lúdico-narrativa en Assassin’s Creed: La Hermandad
ai_summary: This Spanish-language paper uses a hermeneutic approach to examine how the musical topos of 'ombra' (shadow) in the soundtrack of Assassin's Creed: Brotherhood creates an ominous atmosphere, induces alarm and ethical reflection, and shapes players' perception of their environment and play style in line with the game's narrative.

title: Empower Tomorrow's Leaders by Time Traveling to the Ancient World
ai_summary: This chapter argues that integrating Assassin's Creed: Odyssey into college history and classics courses, through game-based assignments and student feedback, can foster critical thinking, problem-solving, adaptability, and historical understanding.

title: Ethical Gameplay
ai_summary: This chapter uses the 'Blood Fever' mission in Assassin's Creed Odyssey as a starting point for examining morality systems and ethical dilemmas in games, drawing on Rittel and Webber's 'wicked problems' (as adapted by Sicart) to classify dilemmas from tame to super wicked and to argue that games function as moral laboratories that test player values.

title: Evolution of Arabic video game localization
authors: Al-batineh, Mohammed; Alzaabi, Khadija; Alnaqbi, Amna; Aldhaheri, Maitha; Al-Hassani, Shamma
games: AC1; AC3; Black Flag; Ezio Trilogy; Odyssey; Origins; Syndicate; Unity; Valhalla
tags: #source/auto-retrieved; game:ac1; game:ac3; game:black-flag; game:ezio-trilogy; game:odyssey; game:origins; game:syndicate; game:unity; game:valhalla; lang:en; rel:core; type:research-article
ai_summary: This study traces the evolution of Arabic localization in Ubisoft's Assassin's Creed series from 2007 to 2023, showing how market demand, regional support, and technological advances drove the shift from no localization to full Arabic support, including right-to-left language handling, cultural adaptation, and Arabic voiceovers.

title: Exploring Protagonist Characterization in Assassin’s Creed III (2012): A Transitivity Analysis
ai_summary: Using Systemic Functional Linguistics' transitivity system to analyze dialogue in Assassin's Creed III, the study shows how Connor Kenway's characterization is shaped differently by himself, supporting characters (who portray him as a hero and savior) and villains (who portray him as a criminal and savage), and argues that transitivity is a versatile tool for analyzing characterization in videogames.

title: From Entertainment to Education: An Empirical Study on the Learning Effects of Assassin's Creed in Art History Courses
venue: Journal of Language, Culture and Education
ai_summary: A quasi-experimental study finds that using Assassin's Creed: Origins in higher education art history courses improves students' spatial perception, historical event recall, and cross-cultural comprehension compared with traditional lectures, and proposes a Knowledge, Skills, and Attitudes (KSA) model that integrates academic performance with facial expression data for game-based learning design.

title: Games as a Response to the Cultural Crisis in the Digital Age: Potential and Limitations.
ai_summary: The paper argues that video games, using Assassin's Creed's Discovery Tour and the S.T.A.L.K.E.R. series as case studies, can help preserve, popularize, and reinterpret cultural heritage in the digital age, but only if commercial pressures, AI-generated simplification, stereotypes, and postcolonial narratives are countered by principles of authenticity, critical reflection, and cultural sensitivity.

title: Gamifying the Past: Historical Authenticity, Pedagogy, and Gender Bias in Assassin’s Creed Odyssey
ai_summary: This Master's thesis examines how Assassin's Creed Odyssey represents the ancient past, assessing its historical authenticity, its potential as a pedagogical tool, and the gender bias in its depiction of characters and roles.

title: Gaming as Virtual Experience of Learning Arabic in Native Speakers’ Environment: Assassin’s Creed Mirage
venue: Al-Ta'rib : Jurnal Ilmiah Program Studi Pendidikan Bahasa Arab IAIN Palangka Raya
ai_summary: This study argues that Assassin's Creed: Mirage, Ubisoft's Arabic-themed 9th-century Baghdad game with fully Arabic audio and subtitles, offers a rich, immersive environment for Arabic language learning through in-game dialogue, cultural elements, and NPC interactions, though the authors call for further research to confirm its effectiveness as a learning tool.

title: Gender Stereotypes in Media History: What Gender Identity Is Reproduced in Historical Video Games? A New Analysis of Assassin’s Creed from the Perspective of Historical Education
tags: #source/openalex; game:odyssey; game:origins; game:valhalla; lang:en; rel:core; type:book-chapter
ai_summary: Using a documentary sampling of YouTube cinematic sequences (n = 614), this study analyzes 77 female characters out of 340 across Assassin's Creed Origins, Odyssey, and Valhalla to examine gender stereotypes in historically themed games. It finds a slight increase in female representation, but Eurocentric, patriarchal, and classist perspectives persist, with female roles remaining underrepresented and pinkwashing strategies evident.

title: Gentlewomen, Fallen Men and Caged Birds: Playing with Victorian Myths in Assassin’s Creed Syndicate
ai_summary: This paper argues that Assassin's Creed Syndicate uses a multi-layered, alternating gendered player embodiment to co-construct a neo-Victorian narrative that displaces traditional Victorian myths of femininity and masculinity, such as the Angel in the House and the fallen woman, while revealing how contemporary ideas shape our understanding of the Victorian past and its influence on present-day identities.

title: GUN: Representations of North American Myths and Stereotypes in the Controversial 2005 Western
ai_summary: This article compares the 2005 game GUN with Assassin's Creed III and Red Dead Redemption, examining how their Western narratives and gameplay reproduce American myths and minority stereotypes, particularly in the portrayal of Native Americans. It concludes that GUN, despite its potential to deconstruct these tropes, ultimately perpetuates the genre's common fallacies.

title: Hidden Monsters: Conspiracy Aesthetics in Video Games
ai_summary: The chapter argues that conspiracy aesthetics in Metal Gear Solid, Assassin's Creed, and Tom Clancy's The Division are monstrous because they displace an explicit enemy Other with a systemic monstrous Self, and that this slippery monster has an elective affinity with video games as cultural commodities.

title: Hybrydowa pamięć architektoniczna w grach wideo. Między doświadczeniem realnym a wirtualnym
ai_summary: The article argues that video game architecture produces a hybrid spatial memory, layering real and virtual experiences, and uses the Notre-Dame reconstruction in Assassin's Creed: Unity to show how deliberate anachronisms can make a virtual cathedral feel as 'authentic' and real to players that it entered collective memory after the 2019 fire.

title: Indigenomicon: American Indians, Video Games, and the Structures of Dispossession
ai_summary: Jodi A. Byrd uses Indigenous studies, Black studies, queer studies, and Indigenous feminist critique to argue that games including Assassin's Creed, Animal Crossing, BioShock Infinite, and Demon Souls encode settler governance and dispossession, while their design may also offer routes to resisting Indigenous erasure.

title: Influence des jeux vidéo sur la perception touristique des lieux historiques et culturels
ai_summary: This thesis examines how video games such as Assassin's Creed II, Grand Theft Auto V, and Black Myth: Wukong shape tourism perceptions of historical and cultural sites by fostering emotional attachment, cultural curiosity, and the desire to visit real-world locations, and it discusses the opportunities this creates for cultural and territorial stakeholders.

title: Interkulturell kompetanse gjennom en digital fortelling – Kan et dataspill fostre denne kompetansen?
ai_summary: This Norwegian master's thesis examines whether Assassin's Creed: Discovery Tour: Viking Age, used within a critical literacy pedagogical framework, can foster intercultural competence among upper-secondary English students. Based on observations and assessment results from a designed lesson, the author finds the game has potential as a learning resource, while concluding that classroom use requires careful attention to classroom management, varied teaching, didactic design, and the degree of student autonomy.

title: Jogos Eletrônicos na Educação: criação de um jogo histórico 3D
authors: Rocha, Renan Colzani Da; Araujo, Alexia Silva da Silveira; Andaló, Flávio; Romeiro, N. C.; Leal, Gabriela Zanella; Zanini, L.; Vidal, Vinícius Gil; Vieira, Milton Luiz Horn
ai_summary: The paper proposes a framework for educational game design grounded in psychological theory, built around challenge, fantasy/narrative, and curiosity, and uses the Assassin's Creed series' use of historical narrative as a model for a 3D game set in 1950s Florianópolis centered on folklorist Franklin Cascaes.

title: L’Histoire est notre terrain de jeu : authenticité, fiction et enjeux de représentations dans Assassin’s Creed Mirage
ai_summary: This French-language master's thesis examines how Assassin's Creed Mirage shapes collective imaginaries and mediates history, weighing the tension between historical fidelity and narrative freedom through Baudrillard's concept of hyperreality. It argues that the game's reconstructions go beyond questions of plausibility, reconfiguring players' relationship to the past, influencing collective memory, and contributing to cultural transmission.

title: L’héritage de Praxilla et la philosophie de l’Assassin. Enjeux pédagogiques, militants, ludiques et littéraires de l’extension d’Assassin’s Creed Odyssey
ai_summary: This French-language article examines why the Assassin's Creed Odyssey expansion chooses the Greek poet Praxilla as its heroine, arguing that her reception, like that of other Greek women poets, has long served as a pretext for engaged discourse and innovative experimentation, and it analyzes the expansion's pedagogical, activist, ludic, and literary stakes through game studies, didactics, gender studies, and reception theory.

title: Major Risks in the Production Stage of Game Development
venue: Risk Management for Video Game Professionals
ai_summary: This CRC Press chapter examines execution risks in game development production, such as feature creep, integration failures, QA breakdowns, and change mismanagement, using Assassin's Creed Unity, Star Wars Battlefront II, and Telltale Games as examples. It identifies recurring risk patterns and proposes mitigation strategies, framing production as a test of discipline, scope control, and systems leadership rather than heroic delivery.

title: Player Agency Versus Player-Character
topics: Player Experience & Affect; Semiotics & Character Analysis
ai_summary: This thesis examines how player agency over appearance, actions, and growth affects player-character identity and emotional attachment, using a survey of over 200 respondents comparing the protagonists of Assassin's Creed II and Assassin's Creed Odyssey. It finds that attachment is significantly stronger when agency supports the character's identity and weaker when agency undermines it in favour of player freedom.

title: Playing Adewale
ai_summary: This article argues that Assassin's Creed: Freedom Cry uses its portrayal of the Haitian Revolution and the Maroon movement, through Adewale's narrative and empathic missions, to move beyond colonialist historical gaze and allegorically connect 18th-century anti-slavery struggle to contemporary Black civil rights movements.

title: Playing the White Knight: Constructing Masculinity through Violence in Assassin’s Creed II
ai_summary: This paper argues that Assassin's Creed II and Brotherhood cast the player as a heterosexual male 'white knight' whose violence on behalf of women reaffirms an idealized, patriarchal masculinity, drawing on Butler's gender performativity and Bogost's procedural rhetoric, and it offers healthier alternatives for developers.

title: Playing with history
ai_summary: This chapter examines how the Assassin's Creed franchise recreates historical eras, cultures, architecture, and countries, and how players engage with and appropriate that history, using a virtual ethnography of player social networking sites and interviews with 11 players.

title: Powering up With Love
ai_summary: This chapter defines 'ludic' romance as playful, optional dalliances and flirtations, using Assassin's Creed Odyssey alongside Persona 5 and Yakuza: Like a Dragon to show how gamified dating systems reward self-focused player improvement, and argues that these systems can normalise manipulative relationship behaviour drawn from manosphere 'pick-up' advice.

title: Re-Enacting 9th Century Baghdad: Interview on the Narrative and Worldbuilding Aspects of the Past, as Rendered in Assassin’s Creed Mirage
authors: Wilson, James; Luersen, Eduardo Harry; Weyland, Raphaël; Beaulieu, Sarah
ai_summary: An interview with Ubisoft Montréal historian Raphaël Weyland and narrative designer Sarah Beaulieu on how historical subjects shape the narrative structure and worldbuilding of Assassin's Creed Mirage's 9th-century Baghdad, along with insights into game production in the industry.

title: Representasi Sejarah Islam dalam Video Game: Analisis Assassin’s Creed Mirage
venue: Konferensi Nasional Mahasiswa Sejarah Peradaban Islam
publisher: Sunan Ampel State Islamic University Surabaya
ai_summary: This study examines how Assassin's Creed Mirage represents 9th-century Abbasid Baghdad, finding that its depiction of social and cultural life is largely accurate despite fictional elements added for narrative purposes, and argues that the game has potential as an interactive, nonformal medium for learning Islamic history.

title: Representing history in video games: Reflecting on the development of French historiography of the French Revolution in Assassin's Creed Unity
ai_summary: This thesis examines how Assassin's Creed Unity portrays the French Revolution by testing whether its commemorative sequences, mechanics, and player agency reflect the main trends of French historiography (republican, Marxist, liberal, conservative, revisionist, and postmodern) and how these interpretations interact with the ergodic properties of the game medium.

title: RETRANSMISSION OF FOLKLORE IN VIDEO GAMES: SHANTI SONGS IN THE GAMES «ASSASSIN’S CREED IV: BLACK FLAG» AND «ASSASSIN’S CREED ODYSSEY»
venue: Scientific notes of V I Vernadsky Taurida National University Series Philology Journalism
ai_summary: The paper compares how Assassin's Creed IV: Black Flag reproduces authentic sea shanties with a largely historical performance structure, albeit with chronological anachronisms, while Assassin's Creed Odyssey replaces them with adapted ancient Greek poetry sung in a choral style, prioritizing artistic stylization and immersion over historical accuracy.

title: Runenes moderne liv
ai_summary: This Norwegian master's thesis examines how runes as a writing system are used in 2013–2022 popular culture across the series Beforeigners, the films Frost and The Northman, and the games Red Dead Redemption 2 and Assassin's Creed Valhalla, testing Michael P. Barnes's claim of "mumbo-jumbo runes" and discussing the findings against political and historical uses of runes.

title: Shay Cormac’s Characterization In Assassin’s Creed Rogue Game
venue: MAHADAYA: Jurnal Bahasa, Sastra, dan Budaya
ai_summary: Using Josephson's Six Pillars of Character, this descriptive study classifies Shay Cormac's traits at the start and end of Assassin's Creed Rogue, arguing that he shows responsibility, respect, caring, and citizenship and is therefore a multi-dimensional rather than simple character.

title: The impact of changing graphic settings on performance in selected video games
ai_summary: This study measures how graphics settings such as texture quality, anti-aliasing, and special effects affect frame rates in Assassin's Creed Odyssey, Shadow of the Tomb Raider, and Cyberpunk 2077, and uses the results to offer recommendations for players and developers.

title: The Influence of Bartol's Alamut on Video Game Assassin's Creed and Oliver Bowden’s Eponymous Novel Series
ai_summary: The paper traces the influence of Vladimir Bartol's novel Alamut on the original Assassin's Creed video game and then on Oliver Bowden's novelization Secret Crusade, examining which narrative and stylistic features of Bartol's work are preserved or lost in the transmedia adaptation.

title: The Representation of Aqidah, Ahkam and Akhlaq in Video Games: An Assessment through Content Analysis
authors: Rozi, Yusof Hilmi Bakru; Khafidz, Hasanah Binti Abd
venue: International Journal of Academic Research in Business and Social Sciences
ai_summary: This content analysis of 11 YouTube gameplay videos finds that games such as Assassin's Creed Mirage, the Iblis ruqyah horror game, and a Roblox umrah simulation portray Islamic creed, jurisprudence, and ethics, and it argues that such games can serve as contemporary da'wah tools that support informal religious learning and heritage preservation.

title: The sonic environment of cities in computer games: why it is of interest to sociologists
ai_summary: The paper argues that sound in games such as Assassin's Creed, Mafia III, The Witcher, GTA, and Yakuza functions as an audio archive of history, a medium of emotional memory, and a form of social critique, turning games into audiovisual laboratories for perceiving and interpreting the contemporary city.

title: THE USE OF ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE BASED PRODUCTS IN THE CONTEXT OF TOURISM: THE EXAMPLE OF ASSASSIN S CREED ORIGINS
venue: Journal of Gastronomy Hospitality and Travel (joghat)
ai_summary: This qualitative interview study of 30 university students examines how the Ancient Egypt Discovery Tour in Assassin's Creed Origins shapes young people's travel desire and attitudes toward Egypt, finding that participants' wish to visit Egypt and their positive attitude toward the country increased after playing the game.

title: Ubisofts Assassin‘s Creed Odyssey Discovery Tour – Eine exemplarische Analyse der Passung von Spielinhalten und fachlichen Kompetenzen des Sachunterrichts in NRW
ai_summary: This German-language study examines whether Ubisoft's Assassin's Creed Odyssey Discovery Tour: Ancient Greece fits the NRW primary-school curriculum (Sachunterricht) for teaching time, change, and geographical reflection, and concludes that the tour lacks systematic competence orientation because it was not designed by educators, so teachers must add their own competence-based learning tasks, critical deconstruction of the virtual world, and pre- and post-tour framing.

title: Verschriftlichung Epistemische und sprachliche Grenzen in der Analyse audiovisueller Ereignisse
editors: Benterbusch, Nora
venue: Spotlights on Media Borders / Perspektiven auf Mediengrenzen
ai_summary: This German-language chapter examines the epistemic and linguistic limits of analyzing audiovisual works by applying performance and perception scores to two case studies, the mixed-media installation Playhouse and the opening of Assassin's Creed III, both of which reference opera, and argues that analysis as translation inevitably moves away from its object.

title: Video game opening levels: design & development of an introductory level for an RPG title
venue: RECERCAT (Consorci de Serveis Universitaris de Catalunya)
ai_summary: This thesis designs and builds a playable opening level for a hypothetical RPG, drawing on the design, engagement, and level-production practices of God of War, Ghost of Tsushima, and Assassin's Creed Shadows, which serve as comparative case studies.

title: Video Games as a Tool for Shaping Political Perception in the Digital Era
ai_summary: This paper argues that video games, including Assassin's Creed: Unity, function as active platforms of political socialization that test freedom, moral choice, and power, shaping players' worldviews, collective identity, and ideological norms in the digital era.

title: Video Games, Literature, and Close Playing: A Practical Guide
authors: Chang, Edmond Y.; Welsh, Timothy J.
ai_summary: This practical guide uses 24 case studies of mainstream and independent video games, including Assassin's Creed, to introduce key concepts from video game and literary studies and provides classroom prompts, activities, and assignments for students and instructors.

title: Visual semiotics and digital game spaces: review of the semiotics of architecture in video games
ai_summary: This review assesses Gabriele Aroni's book on the semiotics of architecture in video games, which applies Umberto Eco's theory of denotation and connotation, Enzo D'Armenio's spatial manipulation, and Brian Upton's ludic sign and anticipatory play to decode reconstructive (Assassin's Creed II), fantasy (Final Fantasy XV), and visionary (NaissanceE) game architecture.

title: ВІРТУАЛЬНЕ МОДЕЛЮВАННЯ І ПАМ’ЯТЬ: ЯК ВІДЕОІГРИ ЗБЕРІГАЮТЬ ПАМ’ЯТЬ ПРО ЗНАЙОМІ ФІЗИЧНІ ПРОСТОРИ
ai_summary: The paper argues that video games, through 3D modeling and photogrammetry, act as virtual archives that preserve real places such as medieval Paris in Assassin's Creed Unity and Chornobyl and Kyiv in S.T.A.L.K.E.R., and that their balance of realism and game design makes them tools for cultural heritage preservation and popularization.

title: ‘As you write your Odyssey…’: An empirical study of Classics students’ play interests and ergodic characterization in historical video games
venue: Convergence. The International Journal of Research into New Media Technologies
ai_summary: An active-play study of ten Classics students who played Assassin's Creed Odyssey for eight weeks finds that their characterization choices were driven by four play interests (ludic, prosthetic, narrative, and referential), which shows how players engage with historical games and argues for active play as a method in historical game studies.

title: “Nothing Is True, Everything Is Permitted”
ai_summary: This chapter argues that Assassin's Creed III and its spin-off Assassin's Creed III: Liberation reproduce colonial logics of digital difference through their Indigenous and Afro-Creole playable protagonists, using settler-colonial history of the American Revolution to show how these games enable players to sidestep the genocide and slavery that founded the United States.

title: “Tu nos trouxeste da escuridão até os deuses verdadeiros”
authors: Silva, Ítalo Eduardo da; Souza, J. D. de
venue: Cordis. Revista eletrônica de história social da cidade
ai_summary: The paper argues that digital media such as Assassin's Creed: Origins – The Curse of the Pharaohs can serve as a teaching source for ancient history, using the in-game steles of Tutankhamun within an active learning methodology to help students discuss Egyptian history and to broaden debate on teaching ancient history through digital media.

title: 9. Entretien avec Sandrine Dubouilh et Nicolas Patin : « Confronter nos savoirs »
editors: Beaucé, Pauline; Leichman, Jeffrey M.
venue: St Andrews studies in French history and culture.
ai_summary: An interview with historian Nicolas Patin and theatre architecture specialist Sandrine Dubouilh reflects on their 'historical gameplay' session, held within the Montaigne in Game educational project at a Bordeaux conference, which used the Theatre of Dionysus in Assassin's Creed Odyssey and the Alhambra Music Hall in Assassin's Creed Syndicate to examine the contributions and limits of games for historical research and teaching.

title: A ARQUITETURA NOS JOGOS VIRTUAIS: UMA ANÁLISE SOBRE A CONSTRUÇÃO DE CENÁRIOS 3D DO JOGO ASSASSIN’S CREED BROTHERHOOD
authors: Ferreira, Emilly Dias Campos; Bernardino, F. S.; Borges, Lígia Cardoso
ai_summary: This paper analyzes the 3D scenario construction of Assassin's Creed Brotherhood, applying Lynch's (1960) and Adams's (2003) architectural parameters to show how urban and architectural elements support spatial immersion in digital games.

title: An educational leap of faith: Exploring the connections between instructional architectures and digital game spaces
ai_summary: This exploratory case study of Assassin's Creed Odyssey's Discovery Tour examines how its digital game space shapes instructional architectures, finding that it mainly fosters receptive and, to a lesser extent, exploratory learning, and identifying the synergies and contradictions between playful and pedagogical design.

title: AS POTENCIALIDADES PEDAGÓGICAS DO VIDEOJOGO ASSASSIN’S CREED ORIGINS NA GRADUAÇÃO EM HISTÓRIA
authors: Nabais, Francisco Manuel Dias; Trindade, S.

title: How Do Historical Games Represent the Past?
ai_summary: This chapter examines how historical games function as histories by presenting the past as problem spaces of player choices and designer-defined models, using Assassin's Creed, Civilization, Age of Empires, and The Political Machine as case studies to show how such games can support critical lessons about the past.

title: Imagining Digital Cities: Freedom and (Non-)Human Agency in Representations of Virtual Realities
topics: Philosophy & Ontology of Game Worlds; Power&Ideology
ai_summary: Fuchs and Lahm compare virtual Los Angeles in The Thirteenth Floor, the emerging cities of Boston and New York in Assassin's Creed III, and the city in TRON: Legacy to show how spatial metaphors and code-based restrictions shape the illusion of autonomous choice in neoliberal, post-industrial virtual urban spaces.

title: Jogos digitais e ensino de história antiga : uma abordagem a partir de Assassin`s Creed Odyssey
ai_summary: This Portuguese-language dissertation analyzes Assassin's Creed Odyssey's depiction of the Peloponnesian War in Classical Greece, examining how the game uses historical sources and the concepts of historical representation and uses of the past, and assesses its potential as a teaching resource for ancient history in basic education.

title: Jogos Digitais e História: diálogos com o passado
authors: Teixeira, Maria Renata; Dores, Francine Brandhuber Oliveira; Neto, Nilo Correia de Queiroga; Sena, Pedro Luiz Teixeira de; Calvo, Júlia
tags: #source/openalex; game:origins; game:other-games; game:syndicate; lang:pt; rel:case-study; type:research-article
ai_summary: This article reports a teacher-training project from the Residência Pedagógica program that uses Assassin's Creed: Rogue, Assassin's Creed: Origins, Assassin's Creed: Syndicate, and Far Cry: Primal to teach historical sources, methods, and the relationship between academic research and game production, and argues that digital games can serve as media resources in history education.

title: Kassandra’s Odyssey
ai_summary: This chapter examines the female protagonist Kassandra in Assassin's Creed Odyssey, analyzing the gap between the game's marketing promises, its structural and narrative limits on her playable agency, and player reception via Steam and social media reviews, to assess whether the game advances or undermines debates on gender representation in historical video games.

title: Le champ historien comme terrain de jeu.La conception de jeux vidéo d’histoire face au « droit de véto » des sources
ai_summary: The paper examines how designers of historical video games, drawing on the development of Assassin's Creed IV: Black Flag and its spin-off Freedom Cry, position themselves at the boundaries of the historian's field, adopting ethical principles and framing their creative responsibilities as cultural artisans in light of the historical materials that act as a 'veto' on their work, and how the design process is accompanied by a narrative about digital practice that explains and legitimizes these choices.

title: Le jeu vidéo, commode soupape pour l’inquiétude humaine ou arme pour s’échapper de la cage ?
ai_summary: The paper examines the growing use of the Assassin's Creed series in history classrooms, where players take on a hero who resists a secret group's dictatorial ambitions across different historical periods, and asks whether such games act as a harmless safety valve for human anxiety or as a tool for escaping that anxiety's constraints.

title: Les jeux vidéo pour dépasser les normes de genre ? Le cas Assassin’s Creed: Entretien avec Fanny Lignon par Marie-Lys Arnette
tags: #source/openalex; game:ac1; game:odyssey; game:syndicate; game:valhalla; lang:fr; rel:core; type:research-article
ai_summary: This interview with Fanny Lignon examines how the Assassin's Creed series has handled gender representation, from the male-only avatar of the first game through the female and equal-combat options of later titles to Valhalla's customizable, changeable gender for Eivor, and asks whether this represents a genuine break with gender norms or merely an extension of their boundaries.

title: Level up with Archaeogaming

title: Mashing Up History and Heritage in Assassin’s Creed Odyssey
ai_summary: The article proposes the concept of 'technocultural mashups' to show how historical games like Assassin's Creed Odyssey recombine cultural heritage into gameplay, and how fan-made trailers, paratexts, and player-generated content let players participate in a networked historical imaginary.

title: On the Affective Reception of Characters: A Response to Nicolle Lamerichs

It uses the controversy around the playable character Kassandra in Assassin's Creed: Odyssey as a case study to argue that understanding contemporary media characters requires examining the affective responses of different interpretive communities.

title: Protagonist to Empathy Machine: Exploring the Interpretive Communities and Affective Reception of Characters

ai_summary: This essay proposes a model of affective reception that combines textual representation with audience emotional responses, drawing on affect theory to treat affect as a dynamic social, political, and temporal process. title: Quand les élèves se prennent au jeu (vidéo). Faire cours d'Histoire-Géographie avec Assassin's Creed Odyssey et Papers, please!

title: Que disent les joueurs de l’apprentissage de l’histoire avec Assassin’s Creed ? Entre authenticité et vérité historique

title: Refusing the Axe
ai_summary: This Jönköping University thesis applies the EPIC (Ethics Practice and Implementation Categorization) framework to Assassin's Creed Valhalla, identifying its ethical teaching strategies and goals, and finds that EPIC is effective for spotting teaching opportunities but limited as an evaluative tool that does not account for conflicting strategies, making it better suited to guiding game developers designing ethics-focused games.

title: SANAL ALANDA MİMARLIK TARİHİ: MODERN VİDEO OYUNLARINA BİR BAKIŞ
ai_summary: The paper compares architectural spaces in Assassin's Creed: Revelations, set in 16th-century Istanbul, with their real-world counterparts to assess their historical accuracy and argue that history-based games shape players' memory and experience of architectural history.

title: SCHLIEMANN'S TROY EXHIBITED
ai_summary: This review assesses a study of Graeco-Roman videogames, including Assassin's Creed Origins, arguing that its broad transmedial account of classical reception is convincing and prepares the field, but that it needs more discernment about when the Classics serve as a frame versus meaningful engagement with the ancient world, and would benefit from interviews with developers.

title: Slave Revolt on Screen: The Haitian Revolution in Film and Video Games by Alyssa Goldstein Sepinwall
ai_summary: This French-language review of Alyssa Goldstein Sepinwall's Slave Revolt on Screen examines how films and video games, including Assassin's Creed: Freedom's Cry, represent the Haitian Revolution, arguing that the best representations show the brutality of slavery and let Haitians tell their own history rather than erasing or trivializing it.

title: Swords, Sandals, and Selfies
ai_summary: This chapter examines why videogame-induced tourism has received little academic attention and argues that sandbox games such as Assassin's Creed: Odyssey can serve as pre-visit visualization tools and hybrid fictional-factual learning environments for exploring historical and heritage landscapes.

title: The Curriculum and Cultural Pedagogy of Medievalism Across Mediated Spaces
venue: American Educational Research Association Annual Meeting (AERA)
ai_summary: This AERA paper theorizes medievalism as a social studies curriculum object and as Hayden White's 'practical past,' using Assassin's Creed, Game of Thrones, and Medieval Times to show how popular and material culture shape historical consciousness and to argue for critical, experiential pedagogy about the medieval past's presence today.

title: The Influence of Historiography and Public Discourse on the Murder of the Family of Nicholas II on the Content of Historical Video Games
ai_summary: The paper argues that Assassin's Creed Chronicles: Russia draws on conspiracy-oriented historiography of the murder of Nicholas II's family, portraying secret societies as regicide instigators, while deliberately omitting its ritual, external-interest, and socio-economic dimensions for marketing reasons and to avoid anti-Semitic accusations.

title: The Semiotics of Architecture in Video Games
ai_summary: Gabriele Aroni combines semiotics and architecture theory to propose an analytical framework for video game architecture, using case studies from NaissanceE, Assassin's Creed II, and Final Fantasy XV to show how virtual buildings and cities communicate with players, shape gameplay and storytelling, and relate to real-world architectural traditions.

title: The The Social Action of Edward Kenway in Oliver Bowden's Assassin's Creed Black Flag
venue: Journal of Literature, Linguistics, & Cultural Studies
ai_summary: Using Max Weber's theory of social action within a literary-criticism methodology, this study analyzes how Edward Kenway, the protagonist of Oliver Bowden's Assassin's Creed Black Flag novel, pursues his goals through instrumental, value-rational, affectual, and traditional actions.

title: Translation Techniques Used in Assassin Creed: Renaissance Novel
authors: Arbain; Nababan, M.; Santosa, R.; Wiratno, T.
ai_summary: This study examines how translators adjust impositive speech acts from the English novel Assassin's Creed: Renaissance into Indonesian, finding that most translators rely on conventional equivalence to produce the most suitable and acceptable target-language meaning for the context, as validated through a focus group discussion with three translation professionals.

title: Transmedia and the Future of Character Studies: A Response to Nieves Rosendo
