title: Video Game Experiential Marketing in Tourism: Designing for Experiences
authors: Rainoldi, M.; Winckel, Arne Van den; Yu, Joanne; Neuhofer, Barbara
venue: Information and Communication Technologies in Tourism
ai_summary: This study argues that video games, using Assassin's Creed Odyssey as a case study, can serve as an overlooked tourism marketing medium, identifying five experiential pillars (game world dynamics, immersion, freedom, character connection, and realism) that shape players' intention to visit in-game destinations.

title: Video games: new ground
venue: Ancient Greece and Rome in Modern Science Fiction
ai_summary: This chapter examines how videogames, including Fallout: New Vegas, Mass Effect, and Assassin's Creed, engage with classical antiquity through their interactive narratives, arguing that games are an underused source of classical allusions and influences.

title: Women in Classical Video Games
tags: #source/openalex; game:odyssey; game:origins; game:other-games; lang:en; rel:case-study; type:book
ai_summary: This book-length study examines how women are depicted in video games set in classical antiquity, from the 1980s to the present, with case studies of Assassin's Creed Origins and Odyssey, addressing historical authenticity, gender, sexuality, race, and tropes to argue that games are essential to reception and gender studies.

title: ΤHE NARRATIVE OF THE GAME SPACE: A PLAYER’S LEARNING JOURNEY
authors: Papavlasopoulos, Angelos; Papadopoulou, Agnes; Giannakoulopoulos, Andreas P.
publisher: International Academy of Technology, Education and Development
ai_summary: The paper presents a question-led, discovery-based learning approach in which students in a Greek university didactics course play Assassin's Creed Odyssey and examine its game space, ludic structures, and narrative through Deleuzian concepts such as deterritorialization and the rhizome, with the aim of fostering critical, self-reflective thinking about space.

title: "And You Didn't Even Look at It!"
ai_summary: The paper examines how Assassin's Creed Origins' virtual replica of the Great Pyramid of Giza, which included two antechambers not yet discovered at the game's release, anticipated real archaeological findings, and it uses this case to analyze the role of historical consultation, architectural expertise, and digital reconstruction in the series' claims to historical accuracy.

title: 2) Medioevo in gioco. Prime riflessioni sul “secolo di ferro” nella più recente produzione videoludica
venue: Middle Ages without borders: a conversation on medievalism
publisher: Publications de l’École française de Rome
ai_summary: This book chapter examines how the tenth century, long neglected by the video game industry, is represented in recent games, using Assassin's Creed Revelations and Rise of the Tomb Raider as case studies to reflect on medievalism and the depiction of the period's military events and figures.

title: A Broken Mirror Held to History’s Face On the Narrative Use of Computer Screens, Multi Screen Experiences, and a Transmedia Theoretical Console in the Popular Assassin’s Creed Series
ai_summary: Using Nanna Verhoeff's concept of the theoretical console, this paper argues that Assassin's Creed IV: Black Flag and its series peers assemble computer screens, a second-screen mobile app, and social media into a transmedia constellation that encourages players to contemplate and theorize history in everyday life.

title: A Power Shrouded in Petticoats and Lace: The Representation of Gender Roles in Assassin’s Creed III: Liberation
ai_summary: This article uses Assassin's Creed III: Liberation as a case study to examine how the game's narrative conceptualizes gender, race, and gender performance from an intersectional perspective, arguing that it reproduces stereotypical gender roles and fails to address the protagonist's skin color within the historical setting it seeks to recreate.

title: Analysis of Conditional Clause Translations: Case Studies of Assassin's Creed: Revelations Novel Translation from English to Indonesian
venue: Journal of Research in Business, Economics, and Education
ai_summary: This descriptive qualitative study examines how translator Melodi Violine renders English conditional clauses into Indonesian in Oliver Bowden's Assassin's Creed: Revelations novel, applying Newmark's (1988) translation methods and V diagram to identify the techniques used and whether they emphasize the source or target language.

title: ANALYZING POTENTIAL OF THE ASSASSINS CREED GAME ON HISTORY LEARNING FOR MILLENIAL IN 21st CENTURY EDUCATION
ai_summary: This literature review argues that the Assassin's Creed franchise, whose series are linked to real historical events, can be used as a technology-based medium to increase millennial students' interest in history learning in 21st-century education.

title: Ancient History, what for? Possibilities between Teaching and Entertainment through digital games
authors: Rossi, Andrea Lúcia Dorini de Oliveira Carvalho; Bondioli, Nelson de Paiva
venue: LA Referencia (Red Federada de Repositorios Institucionales de Publicaciones Científicas)
ai_summary: This article argues that digital games can support teaching ancient history by building historical literacy, historical consciousness, and critical thinking, and it analyzes the textual and graphic narratives of Assassin's Creed Origins as a case study of this potential.

title: Assassins, Gods, and Androids: How Narratives and Game Mechanics Shape Eudaimonic Game Experiences
authors: Daneels, R.; Malliet, S.; Geerts, Lieven; Denayer, Natalie; Walrave, M.; Vandebosch, H.
ai_summary: Through qualitative analysis of Assassin's Creed Odyssey, Detroit: Become Human, and God of War, this study argues that eudaimonic game experiences (emotional movement, reflection, and elevation) arise from narrative engagement and narrative- or choice-enhancing mechanics, and that these experiences intensify and evolve across the course of play.

title: Assassin’s Creed III.
ai_summary: The paper examines how Assassin's Creed III structures its conspiratorial Templar-versus-Assassin narrative around Connor, a half-Mohawk, half-British protagonist whose hybrid identity embodies the struggle for free will against Templar order.

title: Assassin’s Creed IV: Black Flag.
ai_summary: This paper examines whether Assassin's Creed IV: Black Flag perpetuates popular pirate myths or helps players understand the complexities of real historical figures.

title: Assassin’s Creed Origins
ai_summary: The paper argues that Assassin's Creed Origins, despite its speculative elements, offers scholarly value through its historically detailed and largely accurate simulation of Ptolemaic and Roman-era Egypt, whose immersive virtual visit deepens players' understanding of ancient Egypt as a real place and supports more robust historical inquiry.

title: Assassin’s Creed Origins Discovery Tour
ai_summary: Drawing on the author's direct involvement as a researcher and writer of the scientific capsules, the paper examines how historians collaborated with Ubisoft teams to build the historical universe of Assassin's Creed: Origins Discovery Tour, detailing the project's ambitions, participants, challenges, strengths, and struggles in relation to historical accuracy.

title: Assassin’s Creed: Freedom Cry.
ai_summary: This paper examines Assassin's Creed: Freedom Cry, the DLC for Black Flag later released as a standalone game, and argues that its historiographical position between fiction and historical reference makes its narrative of masters, slaves, victims, and heroes a significant case for analyzing how games represent slavery and colonial history.

title: Aux armes, citoyens !
ai_summary: The article examines the 2014 controversy in which the French Parti de Gauche accused Assassin's Creed Unity of propagandizing against the Revolutionaries and rewriting history in favor of the Absolute Monarchy, analyzing how Ubisoft's claim that its choices were ludic, the responses of historians, and the press coverage reveal the tensions between ideology, gameplay, historical truth, and French national memory in the representation of the past.

title: Betydningen av autentisitet i representasjonen av fortiden i digitale spill -En undersøkelse av autentisitet i Assassin’s Creed: Odyssey
ai_summary: This Norwegian master's thesis uses a multimodal content analysis of Assassin's Creed Odyssey's depiction of ancient Greece during the Peloponnesian War to argue that players judge historical representation by perceived authenticity, which is shaped by their prior knowledge and expectations, rather than by strict historical accuracy.

title: Broken Games and the Perpetual Update Culture: Revising Failure With Ubisoft’s Assassin’s Creed Unity
ai_summary: The article argues that Ubisoft's broken Assassin's Creed Unity exemplifies how digital producers normalize release-day failure through perpetual beta development, reframe audience outrage as free bug-reporting labor, and use the rhetoric of constant patching to mediate and profit from the instability of digital distribution.

title: Das Mittelalter im Videospiel: ›Assassin’s Creed: Valhalla‹
ai_summary: This German-language paper examines how Assassin's Creed Valhalla depicts 9th-century early medieval England, assessing the game's claims to historical authenticity and its value as a medium for conveying history to a mass audience.

title: Development of Curriculum Guides for the Assassin's Creed Discovery Tour Games to Enhance Teachers' Adoption of Games for Learning
authors: Xu, Chu; Sharma, Robin; Dubé, A.
tags: #source/auto-retrieved; game:odyssey; game:origins; game:valhalla; lang:en; rel:core; type:conference-paper
ai_summary: The paper presents a methodological model for developing curriculum guides for the Assassin's Creed Discovery Tour games, covering curriculum alignment, in-game activities, lesson plans, and technical FAQs, and tests through a post-test-only experiment with 120 in-service teachers whether the guides improve TPACK and TAM and thus teachers' adoption of games for learning.

title: Du jeu vidéo au document de travail : la scolarisation d’ Assassin’s Creed
games: AC1; AC3; Black Flag; Ezio Trilogy; Odyssey; Origins; Syndicate; Unity; Valhalla
tags: #source/openalex; game:ac1; game:ac3; game:black-flag; game:ezio-trilogy; game:odyssey; game:origins; game:syndicate; game:unity; game:valhalla; lang:fr; rel:core; type:research-article
ai_summary: This paper examines how Assassin's Creed, a historical action-adventure franchise, is repurposed as a teaching resource in history-geography classrooms, arguing that studying it as a medium rather than a game reveals its 'deludification' (loss of its ludic character) when it enters the school setting, based on a classroom observation in a French collège.

title: Exploring Player Understandings of Historical Accuracy and Historical Authenticity in Video Games
ai_summary: Through qualitative analysis of 959 forum comments and a survey of 88 Assassin's Creed players, this study finds that players value historical accuracy but often conflate historical authenticity with it (43% equated the two), and it proposes a player-centred definition of historical authenticity with practical implications for developers and publishers.

title: Game Studies. Aproximaciones metodológicas desde la historia del Arte Medieval: (English version)
venue: Espacio Tiempo y Forma Serie VII Historia del Arte
ai_summary: This article reviews the state of research on videogames as cultural objects and argues that the History of Medieval Art can analyze them through the double lens of the historical Middle Ages and the recreated medioevo, using the Assassin's Creed saga, Bloodborne, and A Plague Tale: Innocence to examine medieval and neomedieval architecture in contemporary medievalizing works.

title: Game Studies. Methodological Approaches from the History of Medieval Art: (English version)
venue: Espacio Tiempo y Forma. Serie VII, Historia del Arte
ai_summary: This article reviews the relationship between video games and historical disciplines, arguing that Medieval Art History offers useful methods for analyzing games such as the Assassin's Creed series, Bloodborne, and A Plague Tale: Innocence, whose depictions of medieval and neomedieval architecture form part of the contemporary medievalizing canon.

title: Girls and Assassin’s Creed
venue: Journal of Games, Game Art, and Gamification
ai_summary: This paper applies a feminist interaction design framework to assess how female players experience fulfillment, identity, equity, and empowerment while playing the Assassin's Creed franchise.

title: Heritage Sites and Video Games: Questions of Authenticity and Immersion
ai_summary: This article argues that the player's perception of heritage authenticity in historical settings is intertwined with immersion, proposing a dual framework that maps five forms of heritage authenticity onto five dimensions of game immersion, with Assassin's Creed Unity and its depiction of Notre-Dame as the central case study.

title: HISTORICIDADE INTERSEMIÓTICA – ANALISANDO AS TRADUÇÕES LITERÁRIAS DE ASSASSIN’S CREED SOB A ÓTICA DOS POLISSISTEMAS
ai_summary: Using Even-Zohar's polysystem theory and Plaza's intersemiotic translation, this Portuguese-language article argues that the printed novel adaptation of the first Assassin's Creed (2007) belongs to the franchise's polysystem by integrating the game's side quests and historical content into its narrative.

title: Historiographical operation and videogame design : historical sources in the conception of "Assassin’s Creed IV Black Flag" and "Assassin’s Creed Freedom Cry"
ai_summary: This French-language thesis argues that video game design is a historiographical operation, in which developers' selection and shaping of historical sources for Assassin's Creed IV: Black Flag and Assassin's Creed: Freedom Cry serve both ludic mediation (communicating gameplay rules and mechanics) and historical mediation (representing the past), using the concept of ludoformation.

title: Immersion's Relationship to Enjoyment in Gaming
ai_summary: This UCF dissertation defines immersion, develops an Immersion-Enjoyment Model and survey, and tests it with experienced players of Assassin's Creed Valhalla, finding a weak positive correlation between immersion and enjoyment, with narrative and moral self-reflection as moderators and a call to reevaluate how immersion is defined.

title: Impositive speech act in assassin's creed: Renaissance
authors: Arbain, Arbain; Nababan, Mangatur Rudolf; Santosa, Riyadi; Wiratno, Tri Aru
venue: Journal of Language and Linguistic Studies
ai_summary: This study examines how impositive speech acts (directive, assertive, expressive, commissive, and declarative) function in the tie-in novel Assassin's Creed: Renaissance, using cost-benefit, face-threatening act, and verb-based frameworks, and finds that directives are the most frequent form and that commanding is the main function.

title: Is There a Digital World?
venue: Techné: Research in Philosophy and Technology
ai_summary: Using Assassin's Creed Odyssey as a case study, the paper argues that software experience rests on a radical discrepancy between code and lived experience, that this concealment is a necessary condition of digital experience, and that imagination, through design, recomposes the break between them.

title: L'oltrepassamento della soglia
authors: Rickards, Marco Accordi; Riolo, Manuel Maximilian
venue: Riviste UNIMI (Università degli studi di Milano)
topics: Mythology & Classical Reception; Player Experience & Affect
ai_summary: The paper applies Joseph Campbell's monomyth to the videogame experience, arguing that the player, like the hero of the hero's journey, leaves the ordinary world to answer a call to a magical realm, with Assassin's Creed Valhalla as the main case study for its mythological and heroic elements.

title: Ludotopia. O granicy świata gry
ai_summary: The Polish-language essay introduces 'ludotopia', a dialectical entanglement of game and space, and uses Assassin's Creed Odyssey to show how players inhabit and understand the ludic world through exploration, map reveal, intelligible tags, and renewed narrative motivation, while distinguishing storyworld from gameworld and reconsidering the limits of the game space through the endgame and the concept of horismós.

title: Marketable religion: How game company Ubisoft commodified religion for a global audience
games: AC1; AC3; Black Flag; Ezio Trilogy; Odyssey; Origins; Syndicate; Unity; Valhalla
tags: #source/auto-retrieved; game:ac1; game:ac3; game:black-flag; game:ezio-trilogy; game:odyssey; game:origins; game:syndicate; game:unity; game:valhalla; lang:en; rel:core; type:research-article
ai_summary: Based on 22 interviews with Assassin's Creed developers, this paper argues that Ubisoft's depiction of religion is produced by a de-personalized industrial process that turns religious heritage into a depoliticized, universalized, and science-fictionalized 'marketable religion' designed for a global, secular audience.

title: Mikrotransakce a jejich vliv na design digitálních her
ai_summary: This Czech-language master's thesis examines how paid and free-to-play monetization models and functional and cosmetic microtransactions shape game design and player experience, using ten hours of gameplay analysis across five titles, including Assassin's Creed: Odyssey alongside The Witcher 3, Anthem, Warframe, and Path of Exile.

title: Myth and Suffering in Modern Culture: The Discursive Role of Myth from Oscar Wilde to Woodkid
venue: Our Mythical Hope. The Ancient Myths as Medicine for the Hardships of Life in Children’s and Young Adults’ Culture
ai_summary: The paper argues that the mythical chronotope, which fuses myth and fairy tale through a specific spatiotemporal setting, persists from Wilde and Saint-Exupéry through Marsh's young adult novels to Woodkid's music and its use in Ubisoft's Assassin's Creed series, where it depicts suffering, grief, and rites of passage.

title: Más Allá de la Adaptación. Assassin’s Creed y los Mundos Transmediales
venue: Trasvases entre la Literatura y el Cine
ai_summary: The paper applies transmedia world theory to a content analysis of Assassin's Creed II (video game), the Assassin's Creed film, and the comic Assassin's Creed: Reflections #1, arguing that each medium's affordances shape how audiences migrate across platforms to experience the franchise's fictional universe.

title: Múmias digitais: práticas funerárias em Assassin's Creed Origins
venue: Revista do Museu de Arqueologia e Etnologia
ai_summary: This archaeologically oriented article critically examines how Assassin's Creed Origins represents ancient Egyptian funerary practices, including mummification and burial, and assesses how dialogue among developers, historians/archaeologists, and the public shapes these material representations.

title: Nix y Kassandra: el viaje de la heroína griega a través del videojuego
authors: Martín, Ruth García; Martínez, Begoña Cadiñanos
venue: Cuadernos del Centro de Estudios de Diseño y Comunicación
ai_summary: This Spanish-language paper argues that the Campbellian hero's journey, traditionally built around male protagonists, is reconfigured in Greek-set video games through heroines such as Nix (NyxQuest) and Kassandra (Assassin's Creed Odyssey), whose quests center on family, tradition, and restoring social order rather than purely heroic transformation.

title: Black Flag: What Happened Under the Shadow of Women’s Movement.
venue: SKRIPSI Jurusan Sastra Inggris - Fakultas Sastra UM
ai_summary: This undergraduate thesis from Universitas Negeri Malang analyzes three female characters in Assassin's Creed IV: Black Flag (Mary, Anne, and Caroline) using Connell's feminist theory. It argues that although these women appear to dominate men through their skills, charm, and beauty, they remain dependent on and controlled by men within the game's patriarchal setting.

title: Cruzada Secreta: a construção de uma narrativa ergódica em Assassin’s Creed
ai_summary: This Portuguese-language study compares Assassin's Creed and its spin-off Assassin's Creed: Bloodlines with Oliver Bowden's novel A Cruzada Secreta, arguing that the games' focus on plot rather than on the stealth and sandbox subgenres made their multimodal adaptation into a novel easier.

title: Cultura da mídia e medievalidade: uma análise do videojogo Assassin’s Creed
authors: Porto, César Henrique de Queiroz; Silva, Luiz Gustavo Soares
ai_summary: This paper analyzes the 2007 game Assassin's Creed and its representation of the medieval period during the Third Crusade, arguing that the game's historical narrative reflects the context of its production. It also examines how fans, through media convergence, relate the game's storyline to their everyday experience, drawing on film theory given the scarcity of scholarship on the title.

title: Deferred Normalized Irradiance Probes John Huelin, Benjamin Rouveyrol, and Bartlomiej Wron´ski
authors: Huelin, John; Rouveyrol, Benjamin; Wroński, Bartlomiej
ai_summary: This chapter presents deferred normalized irradiance probes, a partially dynamic global illumination technique developed at Ubisoft Montreal for Assassin's Creed IV: Black Flag, which stores a full 24-hour irradiance cycle in a compressed, GPU-friendly format decoupled from weather and lighting and achieves higher indirect lighting quality than precomputed radiance transfer under open-world constraints across six hardware platforms.

title: ENTRE JOGADOR E LEITOR: ANÁLISE SEMIÓTICA DA ADAPTAÇÃO DE ASSASSIN’S CREED PARA ROMANCE
authors: Júnior, Souza; de, Paulo César Medeiros
ai_summary: Using French Semiotics and game studies, the paper argues that the intersemiotic adaptation of Assassin's Creed II into a novel weakens the original game's persuasive and interactive enunciative strategies, distorting the role of historical events and the unity effect of the series.

title: Everything is Permitted: Redesigning Ezio from Assassin's Creed II as a Female Character
ai_summary: This costume design project redesigns Ezio Auditore from Assassin's Creed II as a female protagonist, Ezia, using Renaissance Italian history and fashion to challenge female archetypes in videogames and to show how historical research can reshape a character's identity, costume, and gameplay.

title: Faut-il avoir peur des jeux vidéo ?
ai_summary: A French historian who advised Ubisoft on the Revolution-set Assassin's Creed Unity offers educators a practical, non-judgmental guide to approaching the game's historical fantasy, including how it compares with other fantasy works that reimagine history.

title: Fru he Neuzeit im Videospiel: Geschichtswissenschaftliche Perspektiven
ai_summary: This review of the German edited volume on history and video games finds that its Assassin's Creed analyses dominate the case studies, criticizes the weak systematic treatment of the early modern era, and argues that historicizing narrative is not unique to digital games but part of a long tradition of historical representation.

title: In de Schaduw van Ezio: Het Mediatoerisme van de Assassin’s Creed Fan
ai_summary: Through online ethnography of Assassin's Creed fan forums, this Dutch-language study argues that fans practicing game tourism construct a 'place of imagination' of Florence, shaped by collective and individual place identities, icons, direct and indirect representations, and the immediate context of the visit.

title: Jean-Clément Martin et Laurent Turcot, Au cœur de la Révolution. Les leçons d’histoire d’un jeu vidéo
ai_summary: This French-language paper examines the controversy surrounding Assassin's Creed Unity, in which political figures and the press criticized the game's ideological portrayal of the French Revolution, and it uses the episode to assess what historical lessons players can draw from the game.

title: Jogos e narrativas : entre a ficção e a história
ai_summary: This thesis examines how Assassin's Creed II and the novel Assassin's Creed: Renascença blend historical discourse with fiction, comparing how narrative is built in the game and the novel and how the player's perspective shapes the game's story. It argues for the versatility of the franchise in merging fiction and history and for its adaptability to the novel form.

title: Narrative Tools for Games
ai_summary: This article applies three narratological concepts, focalization, granularity, and mode of narration, to games, arguing that they function as design tools for producing cognitive meaning-effects in players, with focalization taking a hybrid form, using examples from Assassin's Creed III, Skyrim, Fallout: New Vegas, and Civilization.

title: Textualidad digital y multialfabetización. Los contenidos digitales como material educativo
authors: Valero, Amando López; Martínez, Isabel Jerez
games: AC1; AC3; Black Flag; Ezio Trilogy; Syndicate; Unity
tags: #source/auto-retrieved; game:ac1; game:ac3; game:black-flag; game:ezio-trilogy; game:syndicate; game:unity; lang:es; rel:case-study; type:research-article
ai_summary: The paper argues that hypertextual and transtextual digital content, exemplified by Ubisoft's Assassin's Creed saga, can serve as educational material that reflects the evolution of reading practices from sequential reading to free navigation, and it calls for educational adaptation to digital culture.

title: The Tyranny of Realism: Historical accuracy and politics of representation in Assassin’s Creed III
venue: Loading...: The Journal of the Canadian Game Studies Association
ai_summary: This article argues that Assassin's Creed III's commitment to historical realism is shaped by Ubisoft's constructed notions of its intended player, which limit the game's ability to critique colonial power during the American Revolution and constrain its emancipatory potential.

title: Transmedial Universes: Charting the Heuristics of Media Constellations.
ai_summary: This Utrecht thesis proposes three heuristic models (intellectual property, curatorial, and concept universe) for analysing transmedial universes, using play as an epistemological tool and drawing on Assassin's Creed, Batman, and Slenderman as case studies.

title: Viaja al París 1789 y vive tu propia Revolución Francesa: Assassin's Creed Unity
ai_summary: The paper argues that Assassin's Creed Unity offers players an immersive way to experience the French Revolution of 1789, using interactive play to revive historical events and the turbulent birth of liberty after the Ancien Régime.

title: A3_5 Falling into Straw
authors: McQuade, Gregor; Walker, Michael W.; Garland, Lee; Bradley, T. J.
ai_summary: This physics article examines whether the Assassin's Creed mechanic of leaping from tall buildings into hay bales is survivable, estimating that the depicted bales are safe for falls of about 12-13 m and that the maximum survivable fall height is about 50 m.

title: Assassin's Creed III and the Aesthetics of Disappointment
ai_summary: The paper analyzes prerelease, release, and post-release reviews and commentary on Assassin's Creed III (June 2012 to January 2013) to show how players construct a 'culture of history' around the game, using an 'aesthetics of disappointment' to compare the present with the series' past and future and framing core gamers' pleasure as paidiaic play for 'gaming capital.'

title: Assassin's Creed IV Black Flag: Blackbeard: The Lost Journal
ai_summary: This illustrated tie-in journal presents Blackbeard's and Edward Kenway's in-world diary entries, artifacts, and graphic-novel elements as a transmedia extension that expands the narrative world of Assassin's Creed IV: Black Flag.

title: Costume design in Assassin's Creed III: a comparative study between the real and the virtual
ai_summary: This paper analyzes the physical construction and symbolic meaning of Haytham Kenway's costume in Assassin's Creed III, comparing the physical garment with its virtual counterpart to assess historical and technical accuracy and to offer guidance for game companies designing authentic virtual costumes.

title: El rol de lo videojuegos: análisis y aplicación práctica de la avataridad en el mundo jugable
topics: Game mechanism; Philosophy & Ontology of Game Worlds; Semiotics & Character Analysis
ai_summary: This Spanish-language bachelor's thesis argues that the player and their avatar share the same role, both directed toward the endpoint of completing the game, and tests this hypothesis through analyses of Assassin's Creed: Brotherhood, Grand Theft Auto V, and Contrast, using a central-system model of games and a framework of avatarity.

title: From the Periphery to Center Stage: The Effects and Exploitation of the Other in Titus Andronicus and Assassin’s Creed III
ai_summary: The paper compares Aaron in Shakespeare's Titus Andronicus and Ratonhnhaké:ton in Assassin's Creed III, arguing that both characters are used by the factions they help and then cast out as the 'Other', and that the colonial and imperial dynamics they expose can be examined in video games as well as in early modern drama.

title: Gaming history: computer and video games as historical scholarship
ai_summary: The paper argues that video games can serve as a form of original historical scholarship that rivals traditional monographs, using analyses of game mechanics and narrative structure in history-based games such as Assassin's Creed, Total War, L.A. Noire, Red Dead Redemption, Crusader Kings II, Europa Universalis, and Tracy Fullerton's Walden, and it outlines how a scholarly game could be designed.

title: Ingenting är sant, allt är tillåtet : En kvalitativ studie om historiska datorspel som Assassin’s Creeds påverkan för det oavsiktliga lärandet och dess pedagogiska möjligheter
ai_summary: This Swedish qualitative study interviews 13–15-year-old students, comparing those who played the Assassin's Creed series with those who did not, and finds that unintentional learning from historical games occurs, with attitude and maturity affecting outcomes, and that students broadly support using computer games as an educational tool.

title: JOGOS ELETRÔNICOS COM TEMÁTICAS HISTÓRICAS: REFLEXÕES SOBRE SABERES E APRENDIZAGENS POR MEIO DO ASSASSIN'S CREED
ai_summary: This undergraduate thesis from the Universidade Federal de Santa Catarina reflects on how historically themed electronic games, using the Assassin's Creed franchise as its case, can shape historical knowledge and learning, though the abstract itself contains only institutional metadata, so the argument is inferred from the title.

title: Manifesting Destiny: Performance and the Myth of America
ai_summary: The paper uses Diana Taylor's... (see note) performance theory to show how the American frontier myth, staged in J.N. Barker's The Indian Princess, Mark Twain's Is He Dead?, and Assassin's Creed IV: Black Flag, has shifted from a colonial and theatrical narrative into a historiographic, cyberspace-based one.

title: Moving through space and time: a genealogy of videogame space
tags: #source/openalex; game:ac3; game:ezio-trilogy; game:other-games; lang:en; rel:case-study; type:thesis
ai_summary: This doctoral thesis uses a genealogy of media across four topoi (the railway, the script, the city, and the wilderness) to argue that videogame space is perceived through mediated movement, shaped by player action, offers impossible access beyond physical space, and is structured by cultural narratives, with close analysis of Half-Life, BioShock Infinite, Assassin's Creed II, Assassin's Creed III, and Red Dead Redemption.

title: Playing with Fiction: Ludology and the Evolution of Narrative in Videogames
editors: Stobbart, Dawn; Evans, Monica
venue: Engaging with Videogames: Play, Theory and Practice
ai_summary: This chapter argues that ludology and narrative have coevolved in videogames, producing narrative forms unavailable in other media, and uses Assassin's Creed 2 as a case study to test the contributions and limits of Gérard Genette's Narrative Discourse for analyzing interactive storytelling.

title: Revenge In Oliver Bowden’s Assassin’s Creed: Renaissance Novel (2009): A Psychoanalytic Approach
venue: UMS Library Center of Academic Activities (Universitas Surakarta)
ai_summary: This paper uses structural analysis and a psychoanalytic approach to examine how revenge shapes Ezio Auditore, the protagonist of Oliver Bowden's Assassin's Creed: Renaissance novel, arguing that the novel's structural elements form an inseparable unity and that Ezio's psychological problems drive his pursuit of revenge and his search for resolution.

title: Analysis on the use of Camera Language in Machinima Introduced in 3D Computer Games - Focus on the Tendency of Shot -
ai_summary: The paper analyzes camera angles, movement, and viewpoints in machinima drawn from three 3D games (L.A. Noire, Call of Duty: Black Ops, and Assassin's Creed: Revelations) to identify tendencies in virtual camera use, drawing on film cinematography to argue for applying established visual-art methods in game design.

title: Assassin's Creed III
ai_summary: This abstract presents Assassin's Creed III as a fictionalized account of the American War of Independence, in which the mixed-heritage protagonist Connor catalyzes the revolution and alters the course of history.

title: Assassin’s Creed 2 : - En analys av spelets historiebruk och dess skapande av historiemedvetande
ai_summary: This Swedish-language essay analyses how Assassin's Creed 2 uses history, particularly through its in-game database of historical figures, and argues that this design can stimulate players' historical consciousness and encourage them to seek historical information beyond the game.

title: Comic-Reviews: Assassin's Creed
ai_summary: This German-language bibliographic review covers Assassin's Creed comic adaptations, including the AC1 volumes Desmond and Der Untergang and the AC3 volume Accipiter, showing how the franchise extends into comics as a transmedia form.

title: D. Compagno. Dezmond. Una lettura di Assassin's Creed 2
venue: G|A|M|E The Italian Journal of Game Studies
ai_summary: Compagno offers a semiotic reading of Assassin's Creed II, using a methodologically complex framework to analyze how the game's narrative and characters, including the frame story around Desmond, produce meaning.

title: Digital Gaming Re-imagines the Middle Ages
editors: Kline, Daniel T.
topics: Game-Based Learning & Pedagogy; History Memory; Mythology & Classical Reception
ai_summary: This edited Routledge volume examines how digital games, from tabletop RPGs and Total War titles to World of Warcraft and Dante's Inferno, re-imagine the Middle Ages, and one chapter compares the Templar conspiracy narratives of Assassin's Creed with Deus Ex and Dragon Age.

title: Semi-fictionalized History as Teaching Aids. Opportunities for learning history in Assassin’s Creed II as a digital game and novel
ai_summary: This hermeneutic content analysis of Assassin's Creed II and its tie-in novel Assassin's Creed Renaissance finds that both semi-fictionalized accounts of Renaissance Florence are unreliable as historical sources, and it argues that classroom use requires students to distinguish documentary content from fiction, a skill that depends on prior knowledge.

title: Spiel um historische Authentizität
ai_summary: This German-language Vienna dissertation uses Assassin's Creed as its central case study to examine how the game constructs historical authenticity as a commercially negotiated value, tracing its media-historical precursors (from board-game and sandbox war simulations to film and adventure narratives) and its relationship to national historiographical narratives.

title: THE ROLE OF EZIO’S STRUGGLE IN ITALIAN REVOLUTION ERA IN OLIVER BOWDEN’S ASSASSIN’S CREED RENAISSANCE
venue: Jurnal Ilmiah Mahasiswa Fakultas Ilmu Budaya Universitas Brawijaya
ai_summary: The paper uses a historical approach to argue that Ezio Auditore and his allies drive the revolutionary struggle for freedom and justice in Oliver Bowden's Assassin's Creed Renaissance, and it compares the novel's Assassin-Templar conflicts with the historical record to show how fiction and fact combine.

title: TV-spel i nöjesjournalistiken : En undersökning om tv-spel och recensioner utifrån ett genusperspektiv
ai_summary: This Swedish-language thesis examines how video game companies and Swedish newspapers represent masculinity and femininity in the cover art of Assassin's Creed III, Grand Theft Auto V, Bayonetta, and Tomb Raider, analyzing how gender is constructed in both game marketing and entertainment journalism reviews.

title: “Não é a mesma coisa traduzir Assassin’s Creed e Dora: a exploradora”, de Santiago G. Sanz e Alba C. Porrúa
authors: Hoffmann, Grasiele Fernandes; Rolón, Verônica Rosarito Ramirez Parquet
venue: In-Traduções Revista do Programa de Pós-Graduação em Estudos da Tradução da UFSC
ai_summary: This Portuguese-language interview, originally conducted by Alba C. Porrúa and translated for Brazilian readers, presents a game localizer's perspective on translating Assassin's Creed and contrasts it with children's media localization, drawing attention to game localization as an under-explored area of translation studies in Brazil.

title: Au-delà de « l’envie cinématographique » : le complexe transmédiatique d’Assassin’s Creed
ai_summary: This French-language article examines the Assassin's Creed: Lineage short film trilogy, directed by Yves Simoneau and produced by Hybride Technologies, as a case study of the relationship between cinema and video games. It argues that the films, released free on YouTube to build anticipation for Assassin's Creed II, function as more than promotional tools by drawing on cinematic strengths to expand the franchise, while also exposing the tensions and shared traits between the two media through the paradigms of remediation and transmediality.

title: ESTÉTICA DE LA CREACIÓN VIRTUAL. APROXIMACIÓN A LOS VIDEOJUEGOS EN TANTO QUE DISCURSOS CULTURALES: EL CASO DE ASSASSIN'S CREED
ai_summary: This Spanish-language paper reads the Assassin's Creed series through Bakhtin's concepts of polyphony and the great time, arguing that video games are complex artistic discourses that can reproduce or question the dominant social order rather than serving only as ludic consumer goods.

title: Mittelalter Computer Spiele: Zur Darstellung und Modellierung von Geschichte im populären Computerspiel
ai_summary: This German-language monograph examines how historical computer games such as Assassin's Creed, Anno 1404, and Medieval II: Total War present and model the Middle Ages, asking what counts as a 'historical computer game' and which pasts and historical images these games evoke through their presentational strategies.

title: P2_3 Like Looking for an Assassin in a Haystack
authors: Rogerson, Zach; Walach, Maria‐Theresia; Staab, Daniel; Watkinson, Emily-Jane
ai_summary: This short physics paper uses the elastic compression of wheat straw to estimate the deceleration a character would experience performing the Assassin's Creed 'Leap of Faith' into a haystack, concluding that the stunt would be fatal (about 8000 g).

title: Biotechnology and Science in Video Games: A Destructive Portrayal?
authors: Murdoch, Blake; Rachul, Christen M.; Caulfield, Timothy
ai_summary: This article analyzes how science and biotechnology are portrayed in ten popular video games, including Assassin's Creed, classifying each franchise as presenting science as either constructive or destructive, with a case study of BioShock, and argues that games may influence public perceptions of science in ways similar to Hollywood films.

title: Gaming with God: A Case for the Study of Religion in Video Games
ai_summary: This Trinity College thesis argues for formal scholarly study of religion in video games, examining religious references in the Halo and Assassin's Creed franchises and the public controversies they have provoked.

title: Récit et jeux vidéo : l’exemple du scénario d’Assassin’s Creed
ai_summary: This French-language paper examines the role of narrative in video games through the scenario of the Assassin's Creed franchise, engaging with the narratology versus ludology debate associated with Markku Eskelinen.

title: Assassin's Creed Brotherhood
venue: ACM SIGGRAPH Asia Computer Animation Festival
ai_summary: This paper presents the debut cinematic movie for Assassin's Creed: Brotherhood, introducing its sixteenth-century Rome setting under Pope Rodrigo Borgia, its protagonist Ezio Auditore, and the Assassin Brotherhood's confrontation with the Papal Guard and Cesare Borgia.

title: Play and History: Authenticity and experience in virtual reconstructions and video gaming
venue: OhioLink ETD Center (Ohio Library and Information Network)
ai_summary: The thesis argues that video games set in historical worlds, analyzed through Assassin's Creed, can convey the social context and spatial experience of historic architecture more engagingly than academic virtual reconstructions, and it urges architectural historians to treat such counterfactual, experience-driven reconstructions as legitimate tools for public historical education.

title: Reviews
ai_summary: This two-part review section assesses Assassin's Creed 2 (Ubisoft, 2010) as its lead item, and pairs it with a review of Montola, Stenros and Waern's Pervasive Games: Theory and Design (2009), which examines how pervasive play transforms everyday life.

title: Touchscreens vs. traditional controllers in handheld gaming
authors: Zaman, Loutfouz; Natapov, Daniel; Teather, Robert J.
venue: International Academic Conference on the Future of Game Design and Technology (Futureplay)
ai_summary: This experimental study uses Assassin's Creed: Altair's Chronicles to compare touchscreen (iPhone) and physical-button (Nintendo DS) input, finding that physical controls produced significantly better performance, with fewer deaths and faster completion times, and a gentler learning curve, and that participants preferred them.

title: Assassin's Creed 2
venue: ACM SIGGRAPH Asia Computer Animation Festival
ai_summary: This paper introduces Assassin's Creed II as a direct sequel that immerses players in a recreated 15th-century Renaissance Venice and Italy, following Ezio Auditore da Firenze's quest for vengeance against a secular conspiracy amid the masquerades of the period.

title: Assassin's Creed: Renaissance
ai_summary: This paper examines Oliver Bowden's novelisation of the Ezio storyline, showing how the prose adaptation extends the Assassin's Creed game narrative through Ezio Auditore's revenge plot and the Assassin-Templar conflict in Renaissance Italy.

title: Conceptual Blending in Computer Games: Integrating Fiction and Meaning
ai_summary: This paper applies Fauconnier and Turner's conceptual blending theory to computer games, arguing that games integrate a fictional environment with interactive affordances through a '2½-D' interface, and uses Assassin's Creed as its main case study to show how the on-screen interface refers to a blended hermeneutic space where player and game interact.

title: Assassin’s Creed: A Multi-Cultural Read
authors: El‐Nasr, Magy Seif; Al-Saati, Maha Zeini; Niedenthal, Simon; Milam, David
venue: Loading...: The Journal of the Canadian Game Studies Association
ai_summary: Four co-authors from Middle-Eastern and Western backgrounds and different disciplines (architecture, theatre, computer science) show that the experience of playing Assassin's Creed (2007) is shaped by culture, with Middle-Eastern players responding to its architecture, Arabic language, and nostalgic urban simulations, while Western players focus on architectural beauty, rooftop platforming, and stealth mechanics.
